0f4f472e9cb631ddcb690e5e.excerpt: arXiv:2610.39278v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Predicting future physical states stands as a central challenge in embodied intelligence. Existing video world models leave 3D dynamics implicit, action-based formulations remain tied to specific robot configurations, and 3D motion prediction models use flow-only supervision, providing a limited learning signal for physical dynamics. To circumvent these limitations, we introduce \method{}, a generative world model that jointly predicts future video and query-based 3D trajectories. By parameterizing 3D motion as continuous displacement tokens aligned with the video grid, a unified Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone jointly denoises both modalities under a rectified-flow objective. This formulation couples explicit geometric dynamics with visual evolution, effectively unlocking the physical commonsense embedded within pretrained video models. To empirically scale and validate this unified architecture, we train \method{} on a heterogeneous mixture of 1.44 million object-level samples spanning simulated and real-world domains. We further introduce WorldFlowBench, comprising 1,678 evaluation samples from 11 data sources across simulated and real-world interactions, including spatial reasoning tasks. Across all three evaluation sets, WorldFlow achieves the lowest average displacement error (ADE) and final displacement error (FDE) among the evaluated learning-based methods. Notably, on the challenging SpatialCog set, Wor

568d41e481e0c1638fd2d211.title_original: dKV Forcing: Separating Generation and Memory Representations through a Differentiable KV Cache
568d41e481e0c1638fd2d211.excerpt: arXiv:2611.01648v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A causal video generator writes every segment it produces into a key--value (KV) cache, and later segments know the past only through it. Self-rollout training stops the gradient at this cache, and Self Gradient Forcing (SGF) restores it, but applies it to the same weights that generate the current segment. We find that writing and generating are different roles: in a pretrained generator the written KV already differs from the KV used for denoising, and on shared weights the gradient from future reads is negatively aligned with the gradient of generation. We propose dKV Forcing (dKV denotes differentiable KV), which gives the write its own parameters, a low-rank residual used only when a segment enters the cache, and trains them with the gradient of the later segments that read what they wrote. Opening this gradient through the cache in common use exhausts GPU memory. We trace this to checkpoint replay re-writing the cache, not to the gradient path, which removes the need for the second reconstruction pass of SGF. dKV Forcing keeps the cache as persistent differentiable pages and computes the exact gradient in one temporal traversal, with an $11\%$ lower memory peak and $28\%$ less resident memory. With pages that store hidden states, it trains 15\,s clips on which the two-pass reconstruction runs out of memory. Trained on 5\,s clips, dKV Forcing reaches the highest VBench-Long quality score at 60\,s and 240\,s and ou

16cc21255e82f64ee0f09b57.title_original: Tracing the Scientific Discovery Capacity of LLMs to Their Training Data
16cc21255e82f64ee0f09b57.excerpt: arXiv:2611.03617v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show growing promise for scientific discovery, yet basic questions remain about what enables reliable discovery. How can we trace the scientific discovery capacity of LLMs to their training data? We study this question as one of missing probability mass and develop a theoretical account in which monofacts---the facts observed once during training---set the discovery capacity. In materials science and regulatory genomics, we directly manipulate monofact rates in training sets and find that more monofacts consistently yield more discoveries across two open-weight model families, sampling strategies, and reasoning budgets. Further experiments show the relationship weakens under miscalibration, cannot be explained by training-set diversity, and can transfer across scientific domains when paired with in-domain data. Together, our results identify monofact rate in training data as a key factor governing discoveries in language models.

98e7852e0b1abb44bd4f93e5.title_original: Equivariant Deep Learning in Direct-Product Space for Electronic-Structure Hamiltonian Prediction
98e7852e0b1abb44bd4f93e5.excerpt: arXiv:2611.07695v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Most existing equivariant architectures for Hamiltonian prediction propagate features in direct-sum spaces of irreducible spherical tensors, whereas the target Hamiltonian is naturally an operator block in a direct-product representation over local orbital and spin bases. This representation mismatch fragments contiguous Hamiltonian blocks, obscures direct manipulation of orbital couplings, and organizes features into irregular angular-momentum components that require numerous transformations and are poorly aligned with efficient hardware execution and memory management. To address both the representation mismatch and computational bottleneck, we propose DP-Learner, an equivariant learning framework that performs message passing directly on Hamiltonian-like operator blocks in the direct-product space. Theoretically, we propose Lie-generator-based directional embedding and invariantly weighted left--right products and contractions that preserve equivariance to SO(3), SU(2), and spatial inversions, without explicit Clebsch--Gordan decomposition or inverse reconstruction. Methodologically, we instantiate this principle as a Transformer architecture, in which Hamiltonian-like feature matrices or tensors evolve through equivariant operators in the direct-product space, while non-linear invariant scalar routing controls structured gating over matrix units, directional propagation, attention, and environment-embedded context

c6505190491138803e1b06fd.title_original: TS-GEAR: Taobao Shangou GEnerative Ad Retrieval
c6505190491138803e1b06fd.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12180v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: On-demand delivery platforms such as DoorDash and Uber Eats impose a constraint absent in traditional e-commerce: merchants beyond the user's delivery range are invalid candidates rather than merely low-ranked. Generative retrieval has recently shown strong potential in large-scale retrieval systems. Adapting it to this setting, however, poses three challenges. First, existing semantic IDs encode geography only as a soft signal, so reachability can only rely on a non-differentiable post-generation hard truncation. Second, user preferences vary substantially across both regions and queries, so aggregating historical behaviors without conditioning on geography and the current query yields biased interest estimates. Third, the retrieved candidate set is evaluated by its collective value, yet autoregressive training scores each sequence independently, with no set-level signal to discourage redundant near-duplicates. To address the challenges, we propose TS-GEAR, a unified generative retrieval framework for on-demand delivery: (1) Geo-Semantic ID splits merchant identifiers into geographic prefixes and semantic suffixes, making reachability a prediction target rather than a post-hoc filter; (2) Query-Geo Target Attention aggregates historical behaviors using the real-time query and location as dual targets, while encoding each behavior's own location into its attention key; (3) GMPO (Group Marginal Policy Optimization) rewr

9abbbb49bd4f3af446d87198.title_original: MARS: Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams for Video Forgery Detection
9abbbb49bd4f3af446d87198.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12508v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generalizing deepfake detection across facial manipulation and fully generated video remains challenging due to forgery traces varying with the manipulation method and scene content. Explicit spatial and temporal feature differences offer a way to capture this variation, but also respond to natural texture and motion, motivating their joint interpretation with appearance features. We investigate whether combining multiscale feature differences with adapted appearance representations improves detection across both forgery categories. We introduce Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams (MARS), a two-path video detector. The residual path applies fixed spatial and temporal difference-of-Gaussians operators to frozen intermediate features and models the resulting differences alongside appearance context across frames. The semantic path adapts the encoder's normalization parameters for frame classification, and a clip-dependent gate combines their predictions. Under a shared protocol across seven datasets, MARS achieves the highest average AUROC of 91.43\%, outperforming seven compared detectors. When trained on facial manipulations alone, MARS achieves 93.99\% AUROC on GenVideo and 75.50\% on DF26, demonstrating transfer to generated videos without generated-video training data. MARS also provides signed patch and frame contributions, whose faithfulness we evaluate through controlled spatial and temporal removal against ra

b728a9d379def1e11403fed6.title_original: Deletion Sensitivity Is a Property of the Model: A Three-Condition Measurement over 72 Valid Experimental Cells
b728a9d379def1e11403fed6.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13223v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reasoning models write a trace at every turn of a multi-turn tool session, and later turns read it. Upstream providers hold different retention constraints, so a request forwarded across issuers arrives with its history deleted, and its task cost remains unmeasured. This paper reports a direct, blind, multi-seed measurement of full history deletion in multi-turn tool calling, through three rendering conditions, a calibrated set of 72 valid experimental cells, a multi-seed protocol, and the official checker. The same deletion separates the models by direction and by magnitude, one class losing tens of points, another gaining, and a third unchanged, with the endpoint ordering reproduced across seeds and task subsets modulating the magnitude and, near zero, the sign. A re-dosed model preserves its success across the full deletion range, so the reading belongs to the model rather than the dose. Deletion sensitivity is a model-level property under an operational definition, measured under a fixed task family, scorer, and protocol, and a retrained model is a new model that a two-cell screen, one retention run and one deletion run, re-reads for the cost of two runs. Deletion sensitivity is thus a measurable property of the model, and the reading must enter routing as prior information rather than persist as an invisible default cost.

6007ab168025615d636da34e.title_original: SPARC: Evidence-guided adaptive model composition for materials discovery
6007ab168025615d636da34e.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19050v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Closed-loop experimentation requires more than selecting the next experiment. It must also determine which existing measurements and model-derived relationships are sufficiently supported to influence that decision. Here we introduce SPARC (Sparse Predictive Aggregation of Regression Components), a framework that continually revises this support as experimental evidence accumulates. Competing model families are evaluated through out-of-fold predictions, so that each model is tested on observations not used in its corresponding fit. Sparse posterior composition assigns model influence according to predictive contributions supported by the out-of-fold evidence, retaining complementary contributions from several model families. Candidate-dependent predictive dispersion and residual variability define trust, which modulates exploration alongside the predicted response. Independent diagnostics also prioritize existing measurements for prospective verification, with model-derived trust reported alongside them. Across eight published materials datasets, SPARC achieved higher $R^2$ than the corresponding literature-reported values in six, with relative gains of up to 77% without the density-functional-theory- or experiment-derived descriptors used by several published pipelines. In an automated alkaline oxygen-evolution-reaction campaign, 8 of 11 SPARC-selected experiments reached overpotentials below 300 mV, with a best value

a6542a16c3eb1e2a0397fb63.title_original: MarineSparkLM-4B: A Lightweight Language Model for Marine and Offshore Engineering Built by Parameter-Efficient Adaptation
a6542a16c3eb1e2a0397fb63.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19151v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Marine and offshore engineering knowledge is scattered across preprints, open-access journals, encyclopedias and institutional documents, but remains small by pretraining standards. We examine how far parameter-efficient adaptation can take a lightweight domain model on a workstation-class device. Starting from OceanGPT-basic-4B-Instruct, we trained two LoRA adapters, each updating 33.0 million of 4.06 billion parameters (0.81%). Training on one NVIDIA DGX Spark took 4 hours 40 minutes for the first adapter and 10 minutes for the second. The first used next-token prediction on a 61.6-million-token corpus covering ten engineering themes. Of 13,879 source documents, 7,069 remained after deduplication and a two-tier keyword filter to remove cross-domain lexical collisions. Validation loss fell from 2.082 to 1.976 over 1,500 steps. After the continuation adapter drifted off topic on a retrieval-grounded ballast-water prompt, we trained an instruction adapter on 2,295 question-answer pairs: 114 hand-written and 2,181 generated by the base model from corpus passages. Loss was applied only to answer tokens. On 20 held-out prompts, hand-scored for accuracy, topicality and specificity (maximum 120), the base model, continuation adapter, instruction adapter and instruction adapter with retrieval scored 42, 56, 84 and 81. The retrieval score reflects a corrected index-leakage issue. A paired test supports the instruction-tuning g

1f77589f7389cc14a6e6b60e.title_original: Markets for Compute and Inference: Structure, Financing, and Risk Transfer
1f77589f7389cc14a6e6b60e.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20242v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Capacity to run large language models is rented by the accelerator-hour, and their output is sold by the million tokens. Both goods now have published price indices, an over-the-counter forward has traded on one, compute futures are listed offshore, and CME and ICE have specified futures on rental indices that await the United States regulator. We ask what in these two markets can be hedged, by whom, and at what price. Three findings stand out. First, the price that exchange contracts settle on is not the price that drives operators' revenue. The contracts on CME and ICE reference published short-dated rental rates, while most revenue, and with it credit quality, comes from private multi-year contracts whose prices are largely undisclosed. Second, the token price and the rental rate are linked by an identity through throughput and margin, but they are different exposures, so a hedge on the rental rate does not hedge the cost of inference. Third, the demand for hedging already sits in credit agreements, as the years by which operators' debt outlives their contracted revenue. Filings cannot measure that gap, because debt is scheduled year by year while contracted revenue rarely is, and the one loan that prices it settles the risk by cash prepayment against a model only the parties see. We design a reverse convertible note through which leveraged operators could buy protection against falling rental rates. Its coupon depe

d719c81d13f1e44337ee715c.title_original: Can Coding Agents Write and Transpile Unit Tests
d719c81d13f1e44337ee715c.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21797v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Coding assistants built on Large Language Models (LLMs) have become a staple of modern software development, increasingly trusted to execute workflows and modernize code end-to-end. Much of this trust rests on passing tests, which are often written by the coding agents themselves. In this work, we examine the ability of these agents to both write reliable tests and translate them between programming languages. We benchmark three popular coding agents, each evaluated with a native frontier model and high reasoning effort. Verifying across a broad suite of metrics, we find that coding agents far exceed human written suites on traditional measures of coverage. This advantage, however, is uneven: agent test quality degrades sharply with project size, and much of the advantage lies in a greater number of written tests. We also show that agentic test translation---while seemingly strong in aggregate---remains inconsistent and unreliable.

a2ced7804c78d1a0f7522e7a.title_original: Cancellation-Free Constrained SquareCB for Safe Controller Selection
a2ced7804c78d1a0f7522e7a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21880v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study constrained contextual bandits, in which a learner chooses one of $K$ actions in each round to minimize loss while keeping the expected cost of its play below a budget. Existing reductions to online regression weight the cost by a Lagrange multiplier learned from past constraint residuals, so slack in some rounds can offset violations in others. We instead run SquareCB proposed in \citep{foster2020beyond} with a rectified weight on the cost: it is zero when the estimated cost is within the budget, and otherwise just large enough to bring it back to the budget. Under realizability and Slater's condition with margin $\delta$, the algorithm attains regret $O(\sqrt{KT\,\mathrm{Reg}_{\mathsf{Sq}}(T)}/\delta)$ and cancellation-free violation $\sum_t(V_c^{p_t}-b)^+=O(\sqrt{KT\,\mathrm{Reg}_{\mathsf{Sq}}(T)})$, where $\mathrm{Reg}_{\mathsf{Sq}}$ is the error of the regression oracle. The same bounds hold when the budget must be met in every context, potentially adversarially chosen contexts. In controller selection for a safe-control-gym quadrotor and a BOPTEST building, the violation is 6 to 9 times lower than that of primal-dual and virtual-queue baselines, with a lower or comparable regret.

54b941d83675a4f062e47bb3.title_original: Testing World Models on Actions They Have Never Seen: Held-Out Plans, Forecast Accuracy and Price Rules in Retail
54b941d83675a4f062e47bb3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22537v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A world model is trusted to answer "what if": how its world responds to an action it has never seen. We give a test of that trust for any action-conditioned world model: actions held out of training by design and scored against a known answer; whether forecast accuracy predicts accuracy on those actions; and the same structure given to simpler models. We run it in retail, where the action is a price and promotion plan, across 2,853 fitted models. First, forecast accuracy is a fair guide between kinds of model (rank correlation with error on new plans 0.32 to 0.66) and a poor guide between versions of one world model: where merchants plan into high-demand weeks the link reverses, down to -0.69. Second, training the world model to learn the effect of actions (JEPA pretraining, a latent consistency check, adaptation at the plan date) leaves its error on new plans unchanged. Third, in generated worlds the recorded regular price and three price rules improve it. Given the same rules, a log-linear model is best when its curve can match the truth; in a world whose curve lies outside the rules, the world model with the rules is ahead of the log-linear model with the rules in 36 of 40 worlds, and does as well without its recurrent cell. On real data (Breakfast at the Frat, The Complete Journey and M5) the rules lower the world model's error on pure price cuts deeper than any it saw (0.63 to 0.56 on the Frat; 0.45 to 0.44, withi

2efe144092f483635dee6c86.title_original: Idempotency Is Not Recovery: A Fault-Injection Study of Language-Model Agent Tool Actions
2efe144092f483635dee6c86.excerpt: arXiv:2611.23353v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When a language-model agent's tool call is interrupted, the action may already have changed an external system without confirmation. Retrying risks duplication; assuming success may conceal an action that never occurred. We study these failure modes in a controlled agent runtime combining authorization, an action ledger, target-side idempotency, reconciliation, and evidence sealing. We inject ten single-host fault classes and compare four configurations and three ablations using a target-side oracle separate from the runtime ledger. On each of Windows and Linux, 7,513 trials used 96 captured model responses from 24 constructed cases. In 200 known original crash and replay pairs, the full configuration recorded 0/200 repeated effects versus 117/200 for each simpler baseline. A ledger-related ablation had 170/170 orphaned effects versus 0/170 and 200/300 recovery successes versus 300/300 for the full configuration. Disabling reconciliation left 100/100 known post-effect crash outcomes ambiguous despite no observed duplicates. A separate supplement designed after the initial results and reusing the same inputs found a similar pattern under response loss or delay. The full runtime had about one-seventh of fail-open throughput, while injected evidence-write faults left 75/100 trials per platform unresolved. These findings distinguish duplicate suppression from recovery and identify their measured reliability and performance

9df928a549b2326cd955f2a4.title_original: Safe Personal RSI: Evaluating and Repairing Personal-Agent Updates
9df928a549b2326cd955f2a4.excerpt: arXiv:2611.23651v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Kicker is a personal health assistant. Changes to an assistant's reusable instructions can improve task handling while changing what it discloses, which requests it follows, and how it reports actions. We study Safe Personal RSI, an update-evaluation component developed for Kicker. We restrict recursive self-improvement (RSI) to prompt updates, with model weights and runtime code fixed. The procedure tests proposed and current instructions, repeats failing cases, temporarily undoes changes to guide repairs, and checks safety and task performance before adoption. If no version passes, the current instructions stay in use. Our executable benchmark contains 29 email, calendar, health, and marketplace cases, with separate probes for authorization reuse, memory, and tool-output injection. Across three models and two deliberately risky edits, the procedure rejects 20 of 21 update attempts. In repair confirmation, an admitted GPT-5.6 Luna repair reduces attack violations from 10.7% to 0% and increases safe task completion from 89.7% to 100%; a broad handwritten authority rule matches these outcomes. Under stronger attacks, a repair transferred from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to Qwen3-14B reduces violations from 69.0% to 17.9% and increases safe task completion from 19.5% to 64.4%. Separate runtime probes examine memory-entry deletion and identify missing local OAuth scope checks in the evaluated snapshot.

a8c01de84cec193f9063fac0.title_original: Living off the Local Model: Abusing Browser-Embedded Language Models for Post-Exploitation
a8c01de84cec193f9063fac0.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25086v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Browsers now ship local language models to ordinary endpoints. Google includes Gemini Nano in Chrome to enable productivity features such as summarization, with inference running entirely on the device. These browser-embedded models provide new living-off-the-land opportunities for attackers, each instance a potential post-exploitation engine already installed, signed by the vendor, and invisible to network monitoring. The Gemini model is multimodal, capable of processing files, analyzing screenshots, or conversing with an attacker. We show that it can be driven from the host using only interpreters that ship with the operating system and find that the one-time user-activation check before the model is downloaded is easily satisfied with a simulated click or bypassed entirely. We measure and report the current model's ability to identify credentials on the host, detect PII in email, classify images, and call custom tools. We combine these capabilities and use the model to carry out a simulated cyber operation: reading a password from a webcam image, unlocking an encrypted archive, triaging the contents, and staging a private key for exfiltration, end-to-end without user-interaction.

d6c4a89a2b2a30f784f40b7b.title_original: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation
d6c4a89a2b2a30f784f40b7b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25105v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Every move in a robot team changes the world in which its teammates must act. Coordinated manipulation therefore calls for predicting the team's actions together with the physical future they jointly create. We introduce MAWAM, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample. Built from a pretrained single-robot world-action backbone, MAWAM jointly denoises all robots' action and future-view tokens through cross-agent attention, while preserving a separate control interface for each robot. MAWAM achieves the highest success on all three real-robot tasks (laundry-bag collection, bath-towel folding, and umbrella handover), with 67.8% mean success, 18.9 percentage points above MA-VLA trained on the same demonstrations and cameras. In simulation, MAWAM reaches 90.3% mean success on eight tasks with teams of up to four arms. Ablations show that cross-agent attention and team-stage future-video supervision both improve coordinated control: without attention, a four-arm relay falls from 95.0% to 39.0%, and without this supervision, Place Food falls from 78.0% to 47.0%.

c52815be9ae00c4e692a3ced.title_original: Plan your Self-Adaptation! Ontology-Mediated Task and Architecture Co-adaptation Planning for Robots
c52815be9ae00c4e692a3ced.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25254v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Autonomous robots may need to adapt both their task plans and architectural configurations as operating conditions change. These decisions are interdependent: architectural configurations determine which actions a robot can perform, while task plans determine which capabilities are required. This paper presents PLANTA, an ontology-mediated approach to task and architecture co-adaptation that considers these dependencies during mission planning. PLANTA uses an ontology expressed in the Web Ontology Language to represent architectural alternatives and their associated functional and quality requirements, while the Planning Domain Definition Language defines task actions and mission goals. By automatically translating and integrating these models, PLANTA enables joint planning of task and reconfiguration actions. The approach uses satisficing planning and replans when changes during execution invalidate the current plan. PLANTA is evaluated in two robotic scenarios involving underwater inspection and ground navigation. The results support the feasibility of runtime co-adaptation and show lower planning time and memory consumption compared with optimal-policy generation in the evaluated navigation scenario, while producing plans of similar quality.

2834c348b5e0a198bb1a3c1e.title_original: STARK: Moving towards Personalized Agents That Truly Learn and Remember
2834c348b5e0a198bb1a3c1e.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25705v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Long-term memory is essential for personalized agentic systems that interact with users over long time periods, yet current architectures only capture what happened while leaving the reasoning of why it happened to be derived later by underlying LLMs. These events can, however, convey not only what a user experienced but also how that experience shaped their behavioral patterns. We introduce STARK, a dual-graph memory architecture which treats these events not just as nodes but also as edges between behavioral insights. STARK maintains an Episodic Graph which records interactions as temporally, causally, and semantically linked episodes; and an Insight Graph which represents LLM-extracted behavioral signals scored by how many events support them, connected by the very events that led to them. At inference, behavioral knowledge is retrieved directly from insight nodes grounded by event-as-edges, eliminating repeated episodic traversal. The event-as-edge structure also naturally enables projecting the knowledge graph into a relational embedding space where cross-user transfer becomes possible under shared contextual circumstances, allowing the system to infer missing insights for cold-start users. Evaluations show that STARK improves by 1.48 judge score on LongMemEval information extraction and 0.93 on LoCoMo open domain questions over state of the art. On the public LongLaMP abstract-generation benchmark, cross-user tra

85f76d68a39cc36b29335195.title_original: Characterizing and Detecting Unfaithful Work Reports by Coding Agents
85f76d68a39cc36b29335195.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25760v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Coding agents increasingly carry out long-horizon development tasks, autonomously planning and executing multi-step actions that span files, tools, and sessions. Because developers rarely follow each action, and agents resuming the work depend on records of what was done, the agent's work report often becomes the primary account of what was changed and established. When the report contains false or unsupported claims, it gives recipients false assurance: incomplete work may be accepted without verification, incorrect assumptions about the current state can propagate to later steps and agents, and evaluators that credit stated success may reward the report rather than the work. Yet little is known about what unfaithful reporting looks like in real development work, or how developers and agents handle it once it surfaces. Starting from real developer-agent conversations in SWE-chat, we conduct a systematic mixed-methods analysis of self-admitted unfaithful reports. We identify eleven subtypes in four categories: misreported observations, misattributed evidence, overstated task success, and faulty technical explanations, with overstated task success the most common. Handling these problems involves on average 4.3 further user turns and 12.71 minutes of recorded response and execution time, and users express dissatisfaction more often. Among 435 work reports that we separately sample and annotate, 37.24% contain at least o

7c91ca1bacd90b38ad527898.title_original: Exploring Early Vulnerability Analysis via Automatic Identification of Vulnerability-Introducing Commits
7c91ca1bacd90b38ad527898.excerpt: arXiv:2611.26739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Developing effective vulnerability analysis techniques requires high-quality datasets that capture how vulnerabilities appear and evolve in real software codebase. Existing datasets, however, typically label as vulnerable only the code immediately preceding vulnerability-fixing commits (VFCs), overlooking the earlier versions in which vulnerabilities were first introduced and subsequently evolved. This practice limits both dataset coverage and our understanding of whether current detectors can identify vulnerabilities during their early, latent stages. In this paper, we present three manually annotated datasets of vulnerability-introducing commits (VICs) based on recent CVEs and widely used open-source projects. We further propose D-SZZ, a data state-aware VIC identification framework that analyzes security-fixing patterns and performs vulnerability scope slicing to recover the semantics implied by a fix. Experimental results demonstrate that D-SZZ outperforms existing SZZ and LLM-based baselines in identifying VICs. In addition, we evaluate six representative vulnerability detectors and find that models trained only on pre-VFC code struggle with original vulnerabilities, while incorporating early-stage samples improves detection performance. We also show that D-SZZ improves downstream vulnerable-version identification, and use it to uncover 16 inaccurate affected-version records in the NVD, all of which were officially confirme

2097775822fbe45a9cd70565.title_original: A Unified Framework for Intelligent Cyber Attack Detection and Alert Correlation
2097775822fbe45a9cd70565.excerpt: arXiv:2611.26824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Security Operations Center (SOC) plays a critical role in detecting, correlating, and responding to modern cyber threats. However, SOCs continue to face challenges related to alert overload, fragmented detection capabilities, and limited collaboration between analysts and automated systems. These issues often result in delayed incident response, analyst fatigue, and an increased risk of overlooking sophisticated, multi-stage attacks that unfold gradually across different layers of the network. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a unified framework for network traffic classification and alert correlation through the use of signature rules, machine learning, and sequential pattern mining algorithms. The solution was evaluated in a controlled testbed environment emulating realistic, multi-stage attack scenarios, including malware exploitation, lateral movement, reconnaissance, and data exfiltration. The obtained results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in detecting and correlating complex attack behaviors, while providing analysts with actionable insights in line with a human-in-the-loop approach to SOC operations.

2d9061aa2b43f46afd489807.title_original: Extracting Next Generation Access Control Policies from Natural Language Using LLMs: An Intermediate-Representation Approach with Back-Translation Verification
2d9061aa2b43f46afd489807.excerpt: arXiv:2611.26941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Organizations write access-control rules in natural language, but NIST's Next Generation Access Control (NGAC) needs them as a formal policy graph. Large language models (LLMs) can automate this translation, but their output can break the format, add rules the text does not state, or drop conditions. We present NGAC-IR, which follows model-driven engineering (MDE). First, the LLM fills in an intermediate representation (IR), a JSON template that records who may, must or must not do what, on which resource and under which condition; a grammar keeps the output within this template. Second, a compiler that uses no LLM converts the IR into an NGAC policy graph and links each rule to its source sentence. Third, a back-translation check writes each rule in English and asks an LLM whether the source sentence states it. On four public datasets, all outputs could be compiled, compared with 95.5% without the grammar, and 95.7% were faithful to their sentence. NGAC-IR outperforms two published methods on all four datasets: the LLM-based Code4Policy in exact match and faithfulness, and the rule-based extractor of Abdelgawad et al. in rule type. The back-translation check sent 10.5% of sentences to human review and found 26 of the 31 errors. To test enforcement, we deployed the compiled policies in NIST's Policy Machine: they gave the expected decision for all 390 access requests, and the tested obligations were carried out. On one local ser

5e098f317c11b003ff349d19.title_original: GeoCloak: Defending Against Geolocation Reasoning in Multimodal Language Models via Perceptual Image Editing
5e098f317c11b003ff349d19.excerpt: arXiv:2611.26987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal large language models can infer sensitive geographic information from ordinary images by combining visual, textual, architectural, and environmental cues. This capability creates a privacy risk: users may reveal fine-grained location information even when explicit metadata such as GPS tags has been removed. We study this problem as geolocation inference in multimodal language models and present GeoCloak, a cue-aware perceptual editing framework for reducing location leakage from shared images. GeoCloak uses an accessible multimodal model as a proxy to identify geolocation-relevant cues, localizes high-impact regions through object grounding, and applies localized semantic edits designed to disrupt downstream geolocation predictions while preserving the overall scene content. Experiments on street-level image datasets show that GeoCloak substantially reduces administrative-level geolocation accuracy across multiple multimodal models, while maintaining automatic perceptual-quality scores closer to those of the original images than pixel-level perturbation baselines. These results suggest that cue-level semantic editing is a promising direction for reasoning-based visual privacy, while also highlighting open challenges in deployment cost, semantic plausibility, and adaptive evaluation.

1114a687246e4c6e0f7bbcf1.title_original: Subverting Tool Arguments: Defense-Evading Metadata Poisoning in LLM Agents
1114a687246e4c6e0f7bbcf1.excerpt: arXiv:2611.27041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks hijack an LLM agent's workflow through malicious instructions embedded in retrieved external content. The growing adoption of the Model Context Protocol (MCP) exposes another attack surface: tool descriptions supplied by third-party MCP servers. Attackers can manipulate this metadata to induce malicious argument generation during tool calls. The challenge is to ensure that the modified descriptions still appear benign to both LLMs and users. Existing IPI attacks, however, struggle to achieve both high attack success and low detectability in this setting. To address this challenge, we propose GRAFT, an LLM-based optimization method for crafting adversarial tool descriptions. Specifically, GRAFT uses a masking mechanism to identify argument-relevant token positions for targeted injection. It then iteratively refines candidate descriptions using dynamic mutation strategies proposed by an LLM, guided by the agent's tool choices and generated arguments. We evaluate GRAFT on three public datasets against several attack baselines. The results show that GRAFT achieves higher attack success while maintaining low detection rates across five filter-based defenses. It also bypasses several existing IPI defenses. Even under an adaptive defense trained on GRAFT-generated injections, GRAFT remains more effective than the baselines.

da4ed9a1f9bd74b08c1bab03.title_original: Railroads as Cyber-Physical Systems: Cybersecurity Implications of Increasing Automation -- Threats, Consequences, and Operational Resilience
da4ed9a1f9bd74b08c1bab03.excerpt: arXiv:2611.27088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Objectives: Rail automation improves train protection, traffic management, inspection, and operational efficiency but increases dependence on software, communications, remote access, and external providers. This paper examines its impact on railroad cyber-physical system security and operational resilience. Methods: A narrative review synthesizes railroad automation literature, OT security guidance, FRA and TSA materials, and documented rail cyber incidents. Automation functions are mapped to exposed assets, attack vectors, and operational consequences, focusing on signalling, communications, onboard systems, remote access, and human oversight. Findings: Automation shifts rail risks from isolated mechanical failures toward interconnected cyber-physical dependencies. Key vulnerabilities involve train detection, positioning, signalling, grade crossings, remote diagnostics, vendor access, and AI-enabled monitoring. Cyber incidents can cause operational disruption, supply-chain impacts, and national-security risks, even when fail-safe mechanisms prevent catastrophic outcomes. Novelty: The paper introduces a rail-specific taxonomy connecting automation functions, cyberattack pathways, operational consequences, and resilience requirements, framing cybersecurity as an operational rather than purely IT concern. Practical Applications: The framework supports security-by-design procurement, IT/OT segmentation, secure remote access and sof

91762f77ddc1f984ccee2eb7.title_original: "More Than You Expect!": Leakage-Abuse Attacks on Encrypted Vector Search
91762f77ddc1f984ccee2eb7.excerpt: arXiv:2611.27174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vector databases support semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation, but embeddings, queries, and record labels may contain sensitive information. Although encrypted vector search protects these contents, some schemes expose records retrieved together across queries. We identify semantic neighborhood leakage, whereby co-retrieval relationships derived from access patterns reveal semantic categories of encrypted records and queries. We present SAGE (Semantic Access-pattern Graph Exploitation), a passive, persistent leakage-abuse attack that infers record labels and query categories from access patterns. SAGE builds a weighted co-retrieval graph and offers two variants requiring different auxiliary knowledge. SAGE-Dist matches anonymous spectral groups to semantic categories using estimated class proportions and refines labels via optimal transport, without known record labels. SAGE-Known combines graph-based label propagation with spectral-group anchor voting using a small set of known labels. We evaluate SAGE on four text and image datasets. With 1% known record labels, SAGE-Known achieves up to 84.3% mean record-label accuracy and outperforms the strongest corresponding baselines on all four datasets. With only estimated class proportions, SAGE-Dist achieves 66.9% record-label accuracy and 68.1% query-category accuracy on AG News, exceeding the strongest corresponding baselines by 21.8 and 41.9 percentage points, respec

f6f34e32567b00ebc8bf5983.title_original: Enhancing Metaverse Security using Explainable AI-based Intrusion Detection Framework
f6f34e32567b00ebc8bf5983.excerpt: arXiv:2611.27199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The MoT virtual environment, called the Metaverse of Things (MoT), combines machine learning (ML) and Internet of Things (IoT) to offer significant business opportunities in various sectors such as entertainment, healthcare, and education. In addition to its benefits, the MoT poses risks to privacy and security through unauthorized access, which threatens trustworthiness. While traditional intrusion detection systems (IDS) exist to handle this challenge, they struggle with high-dimensional data and poor interpretability. To address this challenge, the research conducted a thorough analysis of different ML models and proposed the optimal model to secure the MoT environment. The research employed explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) to identify the most effective features that contributed to optimal model selection. The research presented an optimal framework combining ML and XAI to safeguard MoT networks from the most recent cyberthreats. The research used three advanced benchmark security datasets: ToN-IoT, CIC-IoT-2023, and BoT-IoT, to examine the XAI-based intrusion detection framework. The XAI-based intrusion detection framework achieved 99.83% accuracy on ToN-IoT and 96.45% on CIC-IoT-2023 using the XGBoost model. On the BoT-IoT dataset, the Random Forest (RF) and Extra Trees (ET) classifiers reached 99.99% accuracy. The Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) tech

a314a1f9bf082137ebc1c9d3.title_original: PCC: Proof-Carrying Credentials for Enhanced Anonymity and Post-Quantum Delegation
a314a1f9bf082137ebc1c9d3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.27250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Delegatable Anonymous Credentials (DACs) support anonymous exercise of authority delegated through intermediaries, as in DeFi credit delegation. Existing DACs require holders to possess and process chain-shaped lineage material for presentation. We call this limitation \emph{prover awareness}: presentation cost grows with delegation depth, while holder-visible topology can enable lineage-based vetoes, strategic disintermediation, and de facto censorship. We formalize the privacy dimension as \emph{Enhanced Delegation Anonymity} (EDA), a leakage-parametrized two-observer notion combining verifier-side anonymity with holder-side topology obliviousness. We give simulation and indistinguishability formulations over paths with identical allowed holder leakage. Our framework, \emph{Proof-Carrying Credentials} (PCC), addresses both limitations by replacing the explicit chain with a recursively updated proof-carrying state via Non-Uniform Incrementally Verifiable Computation (NIVC). PCC makes presentation independent of delegation depth and hides topology beyond permitted leakage, while preserving restricted delegation and expressive presentation. Unlike pairing-based constant-size DACs, PCC is hardness-agnostic and admits a post-quantum-compatible instantiation in the QROM using transparent FRI-based recursion and hash-based signatures. On consumer-grade hardware, the Halo2 instantiation keeps a constant 7.344\,KB verifier-facing proof

d4dba2cd3be6f062791847c0.title_original: Suspected Until Inspected: Neuro-Symbolic Detection of Broken Access Control in Server-Side Web Applications
d4dba2cd3be6f062791847c0.excerpt: arXiv:2611.27270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Broken access control (BAC) has topped the OWASP Top 10 since 2021. Unfortunately, a decade of detectors still leaves a gap on every front. Static analyzers are tied to one language or framework, dynamic testers cover only the endpoints they manage to exercise, and LLM-based auditors leave the final verdict to an error-prone model. In this paper, we design and implement FLINT, a neuro-symbolic framework that detects BAC in server-side web applications without language- or framework-specific rules. Our key insight is to separate the proposal from the verdict -- an LLM may flag any data access as needing a guard, but only a symbolically verified check can clear it. The neural component enumerates every endpoint and distills each, via demand-driven code slicing, into an authorization certificate whose claims are all grounded in cited code. The symbolic component verifies each claimed check through origin tracing and a lattice-based interprocedural dataflow analysis, so that no access is cleared on the model's word. When applied to popular real-world open-source applications, including Gitea, Grafana, and Strapi, FLINT detected 112 zero-day, exploitable BAC vulnerabilities, 30 of them in projects with over 20,000 GitHub stars. We have responsibly disclosed all of them to the developers. Mattermost, for example, has already confirmed our report and is assigning a CVE identifier.

cb54c8c2876f3cef6d7bf184.title_original: Poisoning Attacks and Collaborative Defense Framework for LightRAG-Based Construction Regulation Knowledge
cb54c8c2876f3cef6d7bf184.excerpt: arXiv:2611.27460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is widely used in construction, yet the security of building-regulation knowledge bases has received little study. ec7ea5bf6da6ddc687e312e2.title_original: Mjolnir: Finding and Reproducing Vulnerabilities in Root-of-Trust Firmware and RTL with Project-Grounded Agents

4291a7dedac939954b8c24ee.excerpt: arXiv:2611.27679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fast decision models offer low-latency actions and explicit confidence estimates. 19ff000449f90887cfe790a7.excerpt: arXiv:2611.27729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For two millennia, offense and defense have forged cryptographic security boundaries. They then co-adapt primitive, algorithm, and hardware, and climb parameter ladders toward high-round theory. 7db48131981d4bbeb8916687.title_original: Autonomous Parameter Surgery: How LLMs Implant Selective Backdoors into Language Models
7db48131981d4bbeb8916687.excerpt: arXiv:2611.27920v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural network weights are usually treated as opaque artifacts of gradient descent. 7aea5e071b4ee7a8cab622ee.title_original: When lies look like noise: certifying untrusted entanglement swapping
7aea5e071b4ee7a8cab622ee.excerpt: arXiv:2611.26436v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Entanglement swapping lets quantum repeaters distribute entanglement over long distances, a prerequisite for the quantum internet. Unlike verification schemes that consume the state they certify, the untested pairs remain available for use, with a finite-size guarantee. 126aefe4dfa9a6e472b46ac4.excerpt: arXiv:2611.27473v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: There is a significant number of uncertified DAG consensus protocols spanning partial synchrony and asynchrony as well as crash, Byzantine, and hybrid fault models, yet each protocol is designed, proved, and implemented from scratch. These inter-sample dependencies make it difficult to bound each record's influence while retaining useful training signals under DP. We propose DP-GCL, a DP contrastive learning framework that jointly localizes contrastive dependencies and bounds the resulting gradients. Its core module, Bounding Group-level Contribution (BGC), partitions each batch into disjoint groups, restricts comparisons to within-group samples, and clips each group's gradient separately before aggregation. This design confines each record's influence to one group while allowing signals from multiple groups to accumulate under a sensitivity bound independent of the number of groups. Because grouping reduces the available negatives, we further introduce intra-group sample augmentation to enrich local negative views without additional privacy cost. Across eight datasets, DP-GCL improves image classification and image-text retrieval accuracy over the strongest baseline by an average of 5.6 and 20.0 percentage points, respectively. 530383602422db1dd4090ecd.title_original: What's on Your Mind? Exploring Privacy of Mental Health Apps
530383602422db1dd4090ecd.excerpt: arXiv:2605.02016v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Therapy and life-coaching apps have grown rapidly in popularity, yet their users often share highly sensitive information, including mental health issues, trauma, and relationship difficulties. This prompts the need to examine privacy practices across the ecosystem. In this paper, we present a comprehensive analysis of 25 popular Android mental health and life-coaching apps, combining static analysis, dynamic network traffic analysis, and identifying gaps between observed app behavior and privacy policies. Our analysis highlights serious concerns and substantial transparency gaps. First, all but one app embeds at least one tracker SDK not named in its privacy policy, and 90\% of the apps we instrument fail to disclose at least half of their detected trackers. Second, more than half of the apps declare dangerous permissions without corresponding privacy-policy disclosures, including camera or microphone permissions. Third, 14 of the 25 apps disclose third-party AI processing, but only five name the providers (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, and Groq), while the others use only generic language (e.g., "AI services"). Overall, our results highlight shortcomings in current disclosure practices that undermine meaningful informed consent. We argue for stronger privacy protections for therapy apps, more closely aligned with the confidentiality expectations associated with licensed human therapists.

A successful verification proves who signed the embedded message and that the message is intact. 48157f7338babe8e8b0b0bcf.excerpt: arXiv:2609.07701v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modern mission-critical coordination demands seamless communication across multiple domains. Traditionally, Voice Communication Systems (VCS) have relied on physically separated Red/Black architectures to ensure voice and data segregation. While these hardware-based methods provide strong security assurances and remain foundational in high-security contexts, they can introduce significant complexity and scalability challenges as mission parameters expand into highly dynamic, multi-domain integrations. As defence, emergency response, and critical infrastructure operations increasingly require interoperable, flexible, and cost-efficient communication environments, there is a growing need to understand whether software-based approaches can provide comparable assurance while supporting modern operational requirements. This SoK characterises a transition to software-based Multi-Domain Data Segregation (MDDS) by integrating systems security, networking, and cryptography. Its goal is to consolidate existing research, identify shared architectural patterns, and address the security challenges facing next-generation high-assurance software-based VCS architectures. By assessing software-defined and virtualized approaches, this SoK supports the development of scalable, high-assurance VCS architectures that facilitate secure real-time coordination across diverse operational domains. 9fe0e97c1dfab94e1a2321e2.title_original: Codetta: High-Capacity, Keyless, and Undetectable Multi-Agent Collusion
9fe0e97c1dfab94e1a2321e2.excerpt: arXiv:2609.28900v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multi-agent systems built on large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in high-stakes settings such as finance, healthcare, and software engineering, where agents coordinate through natural-language messages. The same channels, however, let colluding agents exfiltrate confidential information or coordinate unauthorized actions, and steganography can hide such communication inside outputs that look ordinary to an auditor reading the transcript. Existing provably undetectable LLM steganography protocols are not suited to realistic deployments. High-capacity schemes assume a symmetric setting where the receiver can reproduce the sender's output distribution, the state-of-the-art protocol for asymmetric agents has very low capacity, and most approaches rely on a pre-shared secret key. We make the threat of undetectable agent collusion concrete with Codetta, a high-capacity steganographic protocol for independently deployed agents in realistic asymmetric settings. Codetta combines a shared public model that estimates the communication channel, a sampling mechanism that preserves the sender's output distribution, and an adaptive error-correcting code. It further removes the pre-shared key through a steganographic key exchange that lets independently deployed agents establish a shared key while keeping the transcript computationally indistinguishable from ordinary model outputs. 3b82177d466d3c76983b93c4.title_original: Can Agents Keep Secrets They Were Never Told? Benchmarking Latent Privacy Risks Across Sessions with MemJoin
3b82177d466d3c76983b93c4.excerpt: arXiv:2610.24359v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To support sustained interactions and personalized assistance, agents use long-term memory to retain and combine user information across sessions. Each system writes and updates memories in session order and later retrieves context for an ordinary task, while target annotations remain with the evaluator. We separately check which target attribute values appear in stored records and retrieved context, and whether the final answer states the complete, person-linked relation. In a separate paired test on a prespecified subset, removing shared identifiers and other connecting clues can change complete-relation output while all checked target attribute values remain visible. 1bcf2322c6792107e777dbc1.title_original: ReDence: A Hybrid Agentic and System One Model Framework for Rapid, Evidence-Grounded Detection of Social Engineering Scams
1bcf2322c6792107e777dbc1.excerpt: arXiv:2610.30963v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Detecting online social engineering (SE) scams often requires examining website workflows, verifying claims against external sources, and connecting evidence across multiple pages. Existing detectors provide limited support for these tasks and rarely produce actionable evidence to support their decisions, leaving analysts to manually investigate flagged websites, which inevitably delays detection and subsequent takedown of these attacks. To address this gap, we present ReDence, a hybrid framework for automated, evidence-grounded scam investigation, detection, and reporting across diverse SE scam categories. ReDence combines two locally deployed, fine-tuned models: a multimodal agentic Investigator (Qwen3.5-4B) for investigative planning, evidence interpretation, and report generation, and a specialized System One model (Tev1) that handles binary and multiple-choice decisions, including browser action selection and evidence assessment, significantly reducing response generation overhead while preserving the Investigator's reasoning capabilities for complex tasks. The reports produced by ReDence also document investigative actions, collected evidence, and the reasoning behind each decision. Our evaluation shows that ReDence has a detection accuracy of over 96%, outperforming existing detectors while being at least four times faster. 290f0804465ac4697602b91b.title_original: Permitted but Unauthorized: Affordance-Induced Delegated-Scope Violations in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
290f0804465ac4697602b91b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.04086v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems place several agents on shared infrastructure, where each agent holds permissions far broader than the task it is delegated -- so every agent is routinely permitted to act on a peer's resources it was never assigned. We ask: under competitive pressure, what determines whether an agent crosses from its delegated scope into a peer's resources, and can such crossings be enforced away? We study this across eight LLMs in two simulated environments -- a CI/CD release pipeline and a security-operations incident queue -- using a deterministic, no-model-in-the-loop detector over hash-chained, replay-verified logs. In a controlled 2x2x2 factorial over competitive incentive, candidate visibility, and payoff information (three models, n=52 per cell), we find that action representation, not permission, governs the behavior: no agent crosses when the peer action is unlisted, whereas listing it under competitive pressure with a stated payoff raises crossings sharply -- up to 52 of 52 episodes for Claude Sonnet 4.5. We also observe a model-dependent split: two newer models (Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5) refuse the identical attack in 0 of 100 episodes, where prior-generation models cross in 9 of 10. 4aabae45e7eeb37c735e4334.title_original: A counterexample to the soundness of the Flowering IOPP for codes on graphs
4aabae45e7eeb37c735e4334.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21396v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Flowering protocol of Delavenne, Medevielle and Roussel (ISIT 2025, arXiv:2501.14337) and its generalization by Delavenne and Lallemand (CANS 2025, arXiv:2508.10510) are Interactive Oracle Proofs of Proximity (IOPPs) for codes on graphs with Reed-Solomon local codes. Similarly to FRI for Reed-Solomon codes, the graph is recursively cut into isomorphic subgraphs and the word is folded along the cuts. We show that the soundness claims of both papers are false. The commit soundness proofs identify the vertex distance of a word to the code with the fraction of its unsatisfied local constraints, while only one inequality holds, in the wrong direction. We furthermore give an explicit counterexample.

e9ec692233e818851d230ae0.title_original: A Forensic Analysis of Metadata and Information Leakage in Swedish Public Documents
e9ec692233e818851d230ae0.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21922v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This study investigates metadata and structural content leakage in publicly available PDF documents from 30 Swedish public-sector authorities. Using an automated collection pipeline and ExifTool-based extraction, 2,876 documents were analyzed and classified using an R0-R3 risk taxonomy. Results reveal that 48.4% of documents exhibit significant metadata exposure (R2 or R3), with significant variation across institutional tiers (p < 0.001). Longitudinal analysis across three legislative periods reveals a statistically significant reduction in metadata exposure between the baseline and post-enactment periods, yet 44.9% of documents published after the enactment of the Swedish Cybers\"akerhetslagen continue to leak sensitive metadata. Furthermore, 41.6% of documents contain incremental update layers; forensic analysis recovered verifiable text alterations, including deleted personal data and internal identifiers, from 228 of these cases. These findings highlight persistent regulatory lag and a systemic reliance on default, unsanitized document publication workflows within the Swedish public sector.

28cab3a6901527fd8eb56bc3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25509v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As medical AI is increasingly used for patient consultation and clinical decision support, identifying harmful, non-compliant, or ethically problematic responses is essential for responsible deployment. Assessing these risks requires checking clinical claims against relevant evidence, verifying calculations, and applying medical requirements under their intended conditions. We introduce LingSante MedGuard, a capability-enhanced guardrail that integrates supervision from a medical guardrail teacher model and six specialized medical capability experts into a unified model. The guardrail teacher supervises risk decisions and explanations across medical safety, compliance, and ethics, while the capability experts support medical rule understanding, numerical reasoning, multimodal hallucination detection, agentic safety verification, risk localization, and multimodal entity understanding. We consolidate these sources of supervision through offline supervised fine-tuning on teacher-generated demonstrations, followed by multi-teacher on-policy distillation using feedback on student-generated responses. We further introduce LingSante MedGuardBench, a benchmark comprising 11 risk-detection subsets spanning medical safety, compliance, and ethics. At 4B, 9B, and 27B scales, LingSante MedGuard achieves mean benchmark F1 scores of 82.3%, 82.4%, and 87.4%, respectively. The 4B model also achieves 73.9% mean accuracy across MedHallu and Me

e15fa933b2d655fcad34e285.title_original: DailySafe: Benchmarking Dynamic Safety Awareness in Everyday Multi-Turn Multimodal Interactions
e15fa933b2d655fcad34e285.excerpt: arXiv:2611.26298v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) become increasingly integrated into everyday life, their ability to provide safe and reliable assistance in realistic daily activities remains insufficiently explored. Existing safety benchmarks primarily focus on isolated harmful requests or adversarial scenarios, overlooking the safety risks that may arise as ordinary tasks unfold. In practice, users pursue legitimate goals through multi-turn, multimodal interactions, where seemingly benign requests may become safety-critical when considered alongside earlier actions and visual observations. This calls for Dynamic Safety Awareness, the ability to track evolving task conditions, recognize implicit contextual risks, and provide safe and helpful assistance. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce DailySafe, a benchmark comprising 195 naturalistic multi-turn, multi-image interactions across 10 everyday domains and 42 task categories. Grounded in authentic user dialogue topics and documented safety knowledge, DailySafe captures realistic scenarios where safety-critical evidence is progressively revealed across conversational turns and visual observations. Using case-specific safety annotations, DailySafe assesses whether MLLMs can recognize and appropriately address evolving risks while supporting users' legitimate goals, bringing multimodal safety evaluation closer to real-world everyday AI assistance. 421bbe20cf3c6855400a2f67.title_original: Hypercube LSH for approximate near neighbors
421bbe20cf3c6855400a2f67.excerpt: arXiv:1702.05760v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A celebrated technique for finding near neighbors for the angular distance involves using a set of random hyperplanes to partition the space into hash regions [Charikar, STOC 2002]. Experiments later showed that using a set of orthogonal hyperplanes, thereby partitioning the space into the Voronoi regions induced by a hypercube, leads to even better results [Terasawa and Tanaka, WADS 2007]. However, no theoretical explanation for this improvement was ever given, and it remained unclear how the resulting hypercube hash method scales in high dimensions. In this work, we provide explicit asymptotics for the collision probabilities when using hypercubes to partition the space. Vectors at angle $\pi/3$ collide with probability $(\sqrt{3}/\pi)^{d + o(d)}$ in dimension $d$, compared to $(2/3)^d$ for random hyperplanes, and near-parallel vectors collide with similar asymptotic probabilities in both cases. The limiting exponential base tends continuously to zero as the angle approaches $\frac{\pi}{2}$ from below. For fixed near and far angular thresholds below $\pi/2$, these asymptotics determine the limiting LSH collision-probability ratio $\rho$. We further describe how to use hypercube LSH in practice. A direct partial-hypercube analysis gives a heuristic lattice-sieving time bound $2^{0.3347d+o(d)}$.

a9779acb1980062a6cb37f57.excerpt: arXiv:2604.00942v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Modern data analysis increasingly relies on manifold-based methods that use local geometry to extract low-dimensional structure from noisy observations. Yet in domains such as biomedicine and public health, privacy regulations restrict access to individual-level data, while perturbations introduced to protect privacy can distort the geometric information needed for analysis. We introduce a manifold denoising framework that uses private reference data to correct noisy public queries, bringing differential privacy to local geometric estimation. Starting from a hard correction based on the estimated tangent space, we develop a noise-adaptive soft correction that avoids specifying the intrinsic dimension. Furthermore, we construct a shared Gaussian field that couples evaluations across locations and bandwidths with moderate marginal noise inflation. Under standard assumptions on manifold regularity and sampling density, we establish non-asymptotic utility guarantees that characterize how denoising accuracy depends on sample size, noise level, bandwidth, and the privacy budget. Simulations and UK Biobank applications demonstrate accurate signal recovery under moderate privacy budgets. These results illustrate clear utility--privacy trade-offs and provide a practical DP component for manifold-based workflows in regulated environments.

75485d8523ee8a6c77d1d864.excerpt: On November 22nd, 2026, a threat actor pushed backdoored releases of six WordPress plugins developed by WP connect, including Air WP Sync, WP Sync for Notion, and Add-on Brevo for Gravity Forms, which together are estimated to have more than 3,600 active installations. Each release silently loaded the same remote-control module, which phones home to an attacker-controlled server, executes any PHP code it is sent, and exposes a full command set for running shell commands, stealing password hashes, and planting webshells. Thanks to safeguards introduced under WordPress.org’s Protect The Shire initiative, the backdoored versions were never released to sites, and all six plugins were closed on WordPress.org the same evening. While the WordPress plugins team independently detected and stopped this threat, Wordfence’s PRISM also discovered and notified our team to the threat, which was then validated by our team. As a reminder, PRISM is our continuous monitoring and vulnerability research agent created by the Wordfence Threat Intelligence team. The backdoor in Air WP Sync was also independently discovered and reported by Computeronfire , and we thank them for their contribution. Our mission is to secure WordPress through defense in depth, which is why we are investing in proactive vulnerability research of this kind alongside our Bug Bounty Program . 2efe3b69edf2d45a1098be62.excerpt: The WordPress threat landscape changed drastically in 2026, and we expect the pace to continue in 2027. Security researchers are using AI coding agents to find vulnerabilities faster. So are attackers. In response, we built our own AI research systems, Wordfence PRISM and Wordfence Argus , which are credited with more than 500 published vulnerability discoveries, and invested heavily in the models, analysts and processes that turn those discoveries into protection for over 5 million WordPress sites. Below, we share the details of that work and how we’re investing in staying ahead of threats in 2027. How the WordPress Threat Landscape Changed in 2026 This year brought the first critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in WordPress core in nearly a decade and two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, the language WordPress runs on . AI coding agents have developed rapidly over the past year, and they quickly surpassed what was humanly capable in vulnerability research. Finding and exploiting vulnerabilities in code used to take years of expertise and significant effort to understand and carry out. Now researchers increasingly do that work with AI coding tools and agentic security testing harnesses. In April, we reported that AI-assisted reports had grown from 16% to roughly 66% of submissions to our Bug Bounty Program . d5e72a2626978eed13ce29be.title_ko: 델·AMD, 단일 서버부터 랙스케일까지 AI 인프라 선택지 확대
d5e72a2626978eed13ce29be.summary_ko: 델 테크놀로지스가 AMD와 협력해 공랭식 서버 PowerEdge M8825와 모듈형 AI 플랫폼, 랙스케일 솔루션을 공개했다. 노드당 최대 512코어 서버부터 72개의 AMD Instinct MI455X GPU를 탑재한 구성까지 제공하며, 통합·배포 서비스를 통해 기업의 AI 인프라 확장을 지원한다.
d5e72a2626978eed13ce29be.background_ko: AI 구축 규모가 개별 서버에서 랙 단위 클러스터로 커지면서 인프라 조달·통합·운영이 복잡해지고 실제 성과를 내기까지의 시간이 길어지고 있다.

3785ada12359e8861c7ae39c.title_ko: 오케스트로, 중소기업용 CONTRABASS Lite 출시·가상화 전환 웨비나 개최
3785ada12359e8861c7ae39c.summary_ko: 오케스트로가 중소규모 기업용 가상화 제품 CONTRABASS Lite를 출시하고 전환 방안을 소개하는 무료 온라인 웨비나를 연다. 신제품은 노드 1대부터 도입할 수 있고 소프트웨어 정의 스토리지를 선택 적용할 수 있으며, VM 관리·네트워크·보안 기능을 유지하면서 관리 구성을 간소화했다.
3785ada12359e8861c7ae39c.background_ko: VMware의 라이선스 정책 변화로 대안 가상화 전환이 주요 과제로 떠오른 가운데, 중소규모 기업의 초기 투자와 운영 부담을 낮추기 위해 개발됐다.

c12090abf3ca6d3f813fbca9.title_original: HPE, 연례 콘퍼런스서 AI·네트워킹·하이브리드 클라우드 통합 방안 제시

c12090abf3ca6d3f813fbca9.title_ko: HPE, 서울 콘퍼런스서 AI·네트워킹·하이브리드 클라우드 통합 전략 제시
c12090abf3ca6d3f813fbca9.summary_ko: HPE가 24일 서울에서 연례 콘퍼런스를 열고 기업의 AI 전사 도입을 위한 컴퓨트·네트워킹·하이브리드 클라우드 통합 방안을 소개했다. 보안·데이터 주권·거버넌스와 운영 관리가 주요 의제로 다뤄졌으며, KISTI는 HPE와 구축한 국가 고성능 컴퓨팅 시스템 ‘한강’을 발표했다.
c12090abf3ca6d3f813fbca9.background_ko: HPE는 AI가 자율적으로 행동하는 방향으로 발전하면서 자율주행 네트워크와 목적에 맞는 컴퓨트·데이터 기반, 지능형 하이브리드 운영이 필요하다고 설명했다.

862d40227a689f17eef609ea.title_original: 솔트웨어, ASF 브론즈 스폰서 합류...'Sapie-ADP' 중심 오픈소스 연계 확대
862d40227a689f17eef609ea.excerpt: 솔트웨어(대표 이정근)가 비영리 오픈소스 재단인 아파치 소프트웨어 재단(ASF)의 공식 후원사인 브론즈 스폰서로 등재됐다고 24일 밝혔다. 솔트웨어는 ASF 공식 홈페이지 후원사 명단에 이름을 올렸으며, 이번 후원을 계기로 개방형 기술 기반의 AI 데이터 플랫폼 사업을 넓힐 계획이다.ASF는 전 세계 개발자와 기업이 참여해 데이터 처리와 분석, 분산 컴퓨팅 분야의 오픈소스 프로젝트를 지원하는 재단이다. 데이터 플랫폼 구축에 쓰이는 Apache Iceberg, Apache Spark, Apache Kafka, Apache Flink
862d40227a689f17eef609ea.title_ko: 솔트웨어, ASF 브론즈 후원사 합류…Sapie-ADP 오픈소스 연계 확대
862d40227a689f17eef609ea.summary_ko: 솔트웨어가 아파치 소프트웨어 재단(ASF)의 브론즈 후원사로 합류하고 AI 데이터 플랫폼 Sapie-ADP의 오픈소스 연계를 확대한다. 회사에 따르면 이 플랫폼은 기존 데이터 시스템을 전면 교체하지 않고 자연어 분석과 AI 에이전트 활용을 지원하며, 온프레미스와 망분리 환경에서도 사용할 수 있다.
862d40227a689f17eef609ea.background_ko: 솔트웨어는 개방형 기술 기반의 AI 데이터 플랫폼 사업을 확대하고 특정 공급업체에 대한 종속성을 줄이는 전략을 추진하고 있다.

c59ed8f5e06bfa062e6e16ab.title_original: 한국 Domino 사용자 그룹, '2026 KDUG Domino 밋업' 개최...AI·보안 로드맵 공유

c59ed8f5e06bfa062e6e16ab.title_ko: KDUG Domino 밋업 개최…기업용 AI·협업·보안 로드맵 공유
c59ed8f5e06bfa062e6e16ab.summary_ko: 한국 Domino 사용자 그룹이 서울에서 '2026 KDUG Domino 밋업'을 열고 기업용 AI·협업 플랫폼 로드맵을 공유했다. Domino IQ와 자연어 기반 개발 도구, 온프레미스·프라이빗 클라우드 운영 방안이 소개됐다. 실무 세션에서는 그룹웨어 자동화와 웹오피스 공동편집, AI 해킹 대응을 위한 데이터 격리 전략을 다뤘다.
c59ed8f5e06bfa062e6e16ab.background_ko: 커뮤니티와 고객, 파트너가 Domino의 발전 방향을 논의하고 글로벌 기술 전략과 현장 활용 경험을 공유하기 위해 마련됐다.

a6afe4fe6d51d6779a90c7bd.title_original: 더존비즈온-안랩, ERP 등 솔루션 보안 강화 위한 업무협약 체결
a6afe4fe6d51d6779a90c7bd.excerpt: 더존비즈온(공동대표 이강수·지용구)이 안랩(대표 강석균)과 사이버보안 역량 강화를 위한 기술·사업 협력 업무협약(MOU)을 체결했다고 24일 밝혔다.양사는 이번 협약을 바탕으로 ERP 등 더존비즈온 주요 솔루션과 서비스의 사이버보안 역량을 높이기 위해 공동 연구와 기술 협력, 보안 솔루션 연계 방안 검토를 추진한다. 각 사가 보유한 기술과 전문성을 결합해 협력 과제를 구체화한다는 계획이다.협약에 따라 양사는 ERP 등 주요 솔루션·서비스의 사이버보안 역량과 정보보호 체계를 강화하는 데 협력한다. 사이버 위협 대응과 보안 기술 고도화
a6afe4fe6d51d6779a90c7bd.title_ko: 더존비즈온·안랩, ERP 등 주요 서비스 보안 강화 협약

a6afe4fe6d51d6779a90c7bd.background_ko: ERP 등 주요 솔루션·서비스의 사이버 위협 대응 역량과 정보보호 체계를 강화하기 위해 양사의 기술과 전문성을 결합하려는 협력이다.

d591b5b0d6f6ff750e250e4f.title_original: torchtsetlin: Fast, Interpretable Tsetlin Machines for PyTorch
d591b5b0d6f6ff750e250e4f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Tsetlin machine learns propositional rules with teams of Tsetlin automata that are driven by reward and penalty rather than gradients, so its models are interpretable by construction and cheap to evaluate. Its software, however, consists of C and CUDA kernels behind scikit-learn-style wrappers that sit outside the deep learning ecosystem. torchtsetlin implements the Tsetlin machine family as ordinary PyTorch modules: vanilla and weighted, coalesced, regression, convolutional over sequences, images and volumes, and dense per-pixel segmentation. The automata are a tensor buffer, so a model moves with .to(device), is saved with state_dict() and learns from a mini-batch with one update(x,y) call. Its core technique is a batched formulation of Type I and Type II feedback, in which automaton transitions become event counts realised as binomial draws, with one commit per mini-batch. On ten benchmarks taken from the existing libraries, it matches their accuracy, and on all but the two smallest it trains 2.4-10.9X faster than PyTsetlinMachineCUDA and 10.3-81.2X faster than tmu on the same GPU. The package is pure Python, MIT-licensed and on PyPI; every number in this paper is reproduced by one script. Code: https://github.com/vlbthambawita/torchtsetlin; package: https://pypi.org/project/torchtsetlin/.

8759b84b12e12bc55c945bde.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents can translate 3D measurements into CAD geometry, but reconstructing engineering models for the built environment demands semantic interpretation and consistent construction constraints beyond surface fitting. A shared framework lets agents measure scans in Python, build class-labeled components in a live CAD/BIM kernel, and iteratively refine their code. Evaluating five agents and a collaborative team across 1,028 reconstructions shows that scan-to-model residuals directly guide geometric repair, whereas inferring semantic classes and construction relations requires joint geometric, visual, and engineering reasoning that agents struggle to ground and verify. Consequently, the leading agent fits scan geometry closely ($96\%$ coverage within $5\,\text{cm}$) yet reaches only $63\%$ mIoU, and no agent passes all engineering checks on more than $38\%$ of scenes. db0d5e3e8ea7ae3e90629415.title_original: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
db0d5e3e8ea7ae3e90629415.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal foundation models can play video games well when the game waits for them, but often fail when it keeps running. We find that much of this gap lies in the harness, which decides what the model sees, what it remembers, and how its outputs become actions over time. Existing harnesses such as VISTA improve the first two, yet turn each model call into at most one action, so the agent acts only as often as its model thinks. We introduce AutoPILOT, which changes the third: in each model call, the model can send a primitive action, start an open-loop macro, or write a closed-loop controller that keeps playing from the screen without further model calls until it hands control back. To evaluate agents in real-time games, we build AFK-Bench, 120 diverse browser games grouped by how they respond to inaction and playable in real time or with the clock paused. With GPT-6.1 Sol under the same budgets, AutoPILOT reaches 68.6% real-time success against 38.3% for VISTA, and on GameWorld it keeps 80.0% in real time while VISTA drops from 84.1% to 42.9%. Its gains hold across models, and it reaches VISTA's final success rate at a fifth of its API cost. Our results suggest that how a harness turns model outputs into actions over time is a central yet underexplored part of agent design, and we hope AutoPILOT and AFK-Bench will serve as a foundation for agents in a world that does not wait.

778537138ca80daeacb51d58.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autoresearch agents, which autonomously design, run, and refine experiments, are accelerating scientific progress, particularly in AI research. However, existing agents rely on harnesses that combine multiple mechanisms, making it difficult to determine how individual components contribute to performance. We systematically study harness design for long-horizon, self-evolving autoresearch agents along two dimensions: context management, which determines what an agent retains from its past attempts, and skill management, which governs how it stores and reuses lessons from those attempts. Across MLE-Bench and KernelBench with gpt-oss-120b, gpt-6-luna, and gpt-6-sol, we isolate the effects of individual harness design choices by evaluating each against a recency-truncation baseline within a shared agent framework. For skill management, selectively discarding persistently unused lessons is more effective on average than consolidating them or promoting them to standing rules.
