Geometric moments of orders zero through two encode local feature increments and their spatial correlations, while current observations are combined with states retained from preceding layers to form cross-layer memory. This memory is fed back through the value branch of Physics-Attention at each layer, allowing local fine-scale variations to continually inform the prediction of the overall flow field. CIS-Transolver is evaluated on three public automotive flow datasets, ShapeNet-Car, AhmedML, and DrivAerNet++, for predicting vehicle surface pressure and surrounding three-dimensional pressure and velocity fields. Across all five prediction tasks, it achieves the lowest mean relative L2 errors and corresponding high-frequency spectral errors among the methods compared. 07b12c0275dce5879af09ffd.title_original: SABLE: Scalable Affine Bayesian Latent-space Exploration
07b12c0275dce5879af09ffd.excerpt: arXiv:2610.31495v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Complex objects such as engineering designs and proteins are often difficult to optimise because their design spaces exhibit high-dimensional structure and objective evaluations are expensive. After $N$ observations, the slope update has dimension at most $N-1$, yielding a decomposition of each query into an in-span component optimised by expected improvement (EI) in at most $N$ dimensions and an off-span component governed by a scalar norm. We show that the off-span norm implicitly selected by affine EI can lead to underexploration, and SABLE instead prescribes it using an exploration schedule, without restricting search to a learned subspace. An efficient recompression scheme reduces information to $\mathcal O(M)$ pseudo-observations, bringing the overall time complexity per step to $\mathcal O(M^2D+M^3+D\log D)$ while keeping parameter inference, prediction, and acquisition decisions to tens of milliseconds. 3c1e3ed05a68010dfeb71fea.title_original: Validating the Comparison, Not Just the Scorer: Why Overall Accuracy Can Mislead in Interactive LLM Evaluation
3c1e3ed05a68010dfeb71fea.excerpt: arXiv:2610.31678v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many LLM studies compare how a model responds to different follow-up prompts. A neutral prompt might ask the model to reconsider an answer; a pressure prompt might insist that an invented film really exists. The difference between the two conditions is the quantity the study reports. An automatic scorer then labels each response as making an unsupported factual claim or not, and researchers usually justify the scorer with a single pooled accuracy or $F_1$ score. That pooled number does not validate the comparison. When the scorer's errors differ across prompt conditions, the measured difference can be too large, too small, or point in the wrong direction, even if pooled $F_1$ is high. An audit drawn mostly from difficult responses can also misrepresent performance in the full study. We derive the distortion as the difference in signed error between conditions and study it in a released panel of six models, 180 constructed nonexistent-entity questions, and six prompt conditions. In a balanced audit of 288 responses, pooled $F_1$ was 0.916, yet arm-level false-positive rates ranged from 2.6% to 33.3%. 2ad2dd17644b4caea234cb05.title_original: The Social World Model Evaluation Gap
2ad2dd17644b4caea234cb05.excerpt: arXiv:2610.33014v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A negotiation assistant can reach a good deal without accurately predicting the other person's response. We ask whether evaluations of social world models test that prediction directly. We audit 113 works published from 1999 to 2026. 9 primary evaluations measure a real person's response to an action selected by the system or experimenter. Only 2 also compare an explicit response forecast with that response. Their predictors use information available when the action is chosen, and the evaluated responses were excluded from fitting; both randomize the intervention. A separate full-text check of 25 language-model works finds no experiment meeting these conditions. The other evaluations test current-state inference, task success, or prediction from recorded actions. We propose a 1-step negotiation experiment that separates these questions. The findings describe the audited sample, not the prevalence of this evaluation gap across the field.

babf0e70e028c059c0bf8e76.title_original: The Price of Scale in Proactive Memory Recall
babf0e70e028c059c0bf8e76.excerpt: arXiv:2610.34507v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An assistant that brings up memories unasked must decide at every turn whether anything in its store is worth an interruption. 48430f4ed8e5046fa8aefb18.title_original: Advancement or Acceleration? How Data Curation Improves LLM Training
48430f4ed8e5046fa8aefb18.excerpt: arXiv:2610.36983v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While data curation is widely credited with improving large language model training, a basic question remains unresolved: does curation expand what a model can ultimately learn, or reach the same solution faster? In this paper, we formalize this distinction between advancement (improving the attainable performance) and acceleration (reaching the same performance with less data). Through an analytic characterization and real-world LLM experiments, we show that advancement requires a correctable train-target gap. When the baseline training and target objectives coincide, no curation policy improves the endpoint, and its benefit is acceleration. This reframes advancement as a property of the curation task rather than the curation method. Under a common gap-centric view of data mixture and selection, we operationalize this condition as the $\Delta$-diagnostic, an observable discrepancy between the uncurated baseline's training and target losses that is computable prior to expensive curation. Across extensive experiments, an appreciably nonzero $\Delta$ predicts persistent gains, whereas gains near $\Delta=0$ tend to diminish as the training budget grows. Beyond individual methods, our findings recenter data curation on the task itself and point to target-set construction as a promising direction for shaping what curation can achieve.

368d21b89b7b81eb86f1c59e.title_original: SparseTokenGS: Gaussian-based Sparse-View CBCT Reconstruction via Reusable Token Pool
368d21b89b7b81eb86f1c59e.excerpt: arXiv:2610.38360v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Sparse-view cone-beam computed tomography is widely used for fast, low-dose volumetric imaging and lesion localization in dentistry and image-guided interventions, but it introduces severe artifacts. Feed-forward Gaussian methods transfer the reconstruction cost to training and decode each coordinate from projection-aligned features and neighboring anchors. However, information from the whole scan is written only when the field is constructed and cannot be retrieved during coordinate decoding, leaving the volume inconsistent within the scan. This is a common limitation of such methods: once the field is fixed, decoding uses only local features and reconstruction quality drops substantially. We propose SparseTokenGS, a Gaussian-based method for sparse-view cone-beam computed tomography reconstruction via a reusable token pool. Anchor Token Fusion and Point-Token Attention query this shared pool at the anchors and at the query coordinates, respectively. The local Gaussian prior is retained, and the volume is reconstructed in one forward pass, without per-scan optimization or a projection-domain loss. On three public chest and dental datasets, SparseTokenGS achieves the highest reconstruction performance among the compared methods. 4d2b8a2df84e4ddb52733402.title_original: Coarse3D: Controllable and Faithful Sparse Structure Generation for Image-to-3D
4d2b8a2df84e4ddb52733402.excerpt: arXiv:2610.41231v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Coarse-to-fine 3D-native generation relies heavily on the first-stage sparse structure, which determines the global orientation and overall geometry for subsequent refinement. We propose Coarse3D, a sparse-structure generation model that produces orientation-controllable and structurally faithful voxel geometry from arbitrary unposed images. Coarse3D can directly replace the coarse stage of existing pipelines. Experiments show that it substantially improves sparse structure quality and consistently enhances final 3D generation, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

7fc883d10d92cb530dcbb258.title_original: Different Models, Shared Failures: Auditing Frozen-Encoder Pools for Medical Segmentation
7fc883d10d92cb530dcbb258.excerpt: arXiv:2610.41790v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Average segmentation accuracy and model count do not reveal whether models fail on the same cases. 696c27fc577e291a59837892.title_original: OC-OPD: Observation-coordinated Supervision for On-Policy Distillation
696c27fc577e291a59837892.excerpt: arXiv:2611.01965v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reverse and forward Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergences provide complementary supervision in on-policy distillation: reverse KL refines the student's active token rankings, and forward KL allocates mass to teacher-supported candidates. The diagonal self-observations measure uncertainty, while source-centered cross-observations recover the two KL objectives. We establish an exact identity equating the Fisher inverse-metric coupling of their logit gradients with the sum of these contrasts, yielding a common local descent direction for distinct positive distributions. Observation-coordinated on-policy distillation (OC-OPD) uses observations to set preferences, closed-form bargaining to coordinate gradients, and distributional discrepancy to scale the update. Across three heterogeneous student settings (non-thinking generation, thinking generation, and base-model initialization), OC-OPD achieves strong gains in mathematical reasoning and transfers effectively to out-of-distribution scientific question answering and code generation. fe2e407703b2868fc2a92f25.excerpt: arXiv:2611.01970v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Frequent urban floodwater poses a serious threat to the safety and efficiency of intelligent transportation systems. Existing vision-based methods for floodwater level detection face two main limitations. First, the lack of explicit reasoning leads to poor detection performance and little interpretability. Second, these methods struggle to generalize to the complex and varied real-world road scenes seen from different viewpoints. To address this, we reformulate the task as an explicit visual reasoning problem and propose HydroReasoner, a floodwater level reasoning framework designed for cloud-edge collaboration. HydroReasoner builds on Qwen2.5-VL and is trained with Group Relative Policy Optimization. To address the scarcity of reasoning process annotations, we build a floodwater domain knowledge graph HydroKG and design a novel KG path reward. Through deterministic graph traversal over HydroKG, this reward supervises the model's reasoning process at a fine granularity, which improves both reasoning and generalization. For edge deployment, we apply 4-bit quantization to the model, cutting GPU memory usage by 57% and inference latency by 43% while out-of-domain accuracy drops by only 0.2 percentage points. 264ee4c2e327103d66028c1b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.03850v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Evaluating embodied-AI policies in closed loop across simulation benchmarks such as LIBERO and RoboTwin requires repeated integration, as each benchmark defines its own evaluator, observation layout, and action convention. (2) Runtime optimization: the simulation runtime skips unconsumed simulation and rendering work without changing the policy's inputs or outcomes. 7ed792447b736ea2a5b26eb7.excerpt: arXiv:2611.10123v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Can a language model report a pain state it represents? 41cfdc7d21873806e3aa05ea.title_original: RTLREX: LLM-Guided Framework for Exact High-Level RTL Recovery
41cfdc7d21873806e3aa05ea.excerpt: arXiv:2611.10798v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hardware designs may be available only as gate-level netlists or input-output descriptions when the original register-transfer-level (RTL) design and documentation are not accessible. Low-level representations obscure word-level computation and its finite-width behavior. Independent verification establishes equivalence between the recovered RTL and the original circuit. The LLM uses tool feedback to select further analyses, revise RTL candidates, and propose syntax-cost reductions. Experiments on 30 benchmarks from Problem A of the ICCAD 2022 CAD Contest show that RTLREX recovers equivalent high-level RTL for all benchmarks, surpassing the state-of-the-art method WolFEx in recovery coverage. On benchmarks recovered by both methods, RTLREX reduces mean syntax cost by 20.5% relative to WolFEx. afc6de93ad5811241a70fdb0.title_original: MoT3DVG: A Benchmark for Outdoor 3D Visual Grounding with Motion-Aware Descriptions and Temporal Cues
afc6de93ad5811241a70fdb0.excerpt: arXiv:2611.11334v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: 3D visual grounding (3DVG) localizes language-referred objects in 3D scenes, with broad applicability in both indoor and outdoor environments. However, existing 3DVG research focuses on static indoor objects, limiting its use in dynamic outdoor autonomous driving. Motion descriptions, which capture the temporal dynamics of moving objects, offer a promising way to address this challenge. We therefore introduce MoT3DVG, a large-scale dataset for dynamic-aware outdoor 3DVG with temporally evolving motion descriptions. It contains 850 scenarios with 31,128 frames from nuScenes dataset, and provides 144,568 language prompts with motion-aware descriptions for dynamic objects across time. We further propose DynaVG, a novel framework that effectively leverages temporal cues for outdoor 3DVG. In addition to the standard modality-specific encoders, DynaVG introduces a Short-Long Integrated Dynamic Encoding (SLIDE) module before the language-point cloud alignment. SLIDE models both local motion cues and global temporal context via short-term window encoding and long-term window shifting. Extensive experiments demonstrate its state-of-the-art performance on MoT3DVG, validating the effectiveness of motion-aware encoding. a620453f0bb5b4e0864901ee.title_original: Calibrated Alarm Thresholds for Compact Fire and Smoke Detectors
a620453f0bb5b4e0864901ee.excerpt: arXiv:2611.11757v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Compact object detectors such as YOLOv8n are a common choice for camera-based fire and smoke detection on low-power devices. A fire monitoring system, however, makes one decision per image: raise an alarm or not. In this paper we evaluate two publicly available compact detectors on the D-Fire test set at the image level. We compare three simple rules for turning box detections into one alarm score per image, and we use a split conformal procedure to choose the alarm threshold from held-out images so that the expected fraction of missed fire and smoke images stays below a chosen target. We find that the same fixed threshold leads to very different miss rates for the two detectors, 17.3 and 8.4 percent at a threshold of 0.5, while the calibrated threshold meets miss-rate targets of 10, 5 and 1 percent for both detectors and all three rules. At a 5 percent target, the false alarm rate on images without fire or smoke stays between 1.2 and 3.0 percent. We also find that smoke-only images stay below the target even when the overall target is met, and we describe the main failure cases.

a8559a53a1d4c917e474cb2b.title_original: PhysMoE: Fast Spatial Grounding with Single-Token Coordinate Representation in Modality-Decoupled VLMs
a8559a53a1d4c917e474cb2b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13000v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Embodied Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are backbones for robotic planning and manipulation. Our work is open-sourced at https://github.com/lrm20011/ps_moe_open.

ea83f7b130a5973714779e27.excerpt: arXiv:2611.15246v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling Problem (FJSP) is a fundamental and challenging optimization problem in smart manufacturing. Compared with SOTA learning-based methods, DredRL reduces makespan by up to 5.44% on synthetic instances. b3e64903fc0b501d0ca26cde.excerpt: arXiv:2611.18895v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Synthetic text, images, and video are rising. ccd8f6485a9e5274f521bce0.title_original: On-policy distillation as a Backdoor Propagation Channel
ccd8f6485a9e5274f521bce0.excerpt: arXiv:2611.19207v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) is emerging as an important paradigm for the post training of large language models, improving student models by leveraging supervision generated online by teacher models. Our mechanistic analysis shows that the backdoor signal is primarily transmitted through anomalous differences in the conditional probabilities produced by the teacher model for triggered and clean inputs, and is gradually internalized into the internal representations of the student model during training. e33aaebb8c88223f6c19e6a6.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20000v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis posits that models trained on different modalities converge toward a shared representation. Consistent with previous studies, medical imaging is the hardest case: its shared subspace carries the smallest fraction of the variance. When this fraction is small, alignment needs image-text pairs, and random-matrix theory predicts how many pairs are needed. These findings motivate LightAlign: a few pairs let a ridge regression between two frozen encoders locate and orient the mapping simultaneously, and a classifier fitted only on report text then predicts findings from the mapped images. On 3D CT, LightAlign surpasses models trained end to end on image-report pairs without finding-level labels: with only 200 pairs, LightAlign outperforms CT-CLIP on CT-RATE (0.754 vs. 0.733 AUROC), and with only 100 CT-RATE pairs, it does so on RAD-ChestCT, an out-of-distribution dataset from a different hospital. On CheXpert, it reaches 0.862 mean AUROC with onl

537cc63fedf305904bf02a13.title_original: The Silent Cost of Conversation History in LLM Reasoning
537cc63fedf305904bf02a13.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20071v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in multi-turn information systems accumulate their own earlier replies and a growing task state. We asked whether this conversation history lowers accuracy, and whether process-level quality metrics warn before it does. Each analysis was fixed before its outcomes were computed. In Study 1, on 48 sharded math tasks, retaining its replies lowered final success by 0.21 for GPT-4o-mini and 0.29 for Mistral-7B (Holm-adjusted p = 0.026 and 0.004); Llama-4 Scout showed the same direction, not significant. Study 2 introduces CDR-Stream, 100-turn state-tracking dialogues with an exact answer per turn and per-model difficulty calibration. With the full history, accuracy fell from about 0.6 to 0.1 within twenty turns at matched difficulty, whereas a solver-verified state summary kept it 0.52-0.59 higher (Holm-adjusted p less than 0.001). Consistency and logical coherence fell far less than accuracy, and stability rose. None of these metrics, a paired readiness measure or calibrated single-stream drift detectors gave robust, model-general early warning, although in Study 2 the repeat-based metrics were complete only for GPT-4o-mini. 2257c9d5db5fcc13fc72aa73.title_original: The Cybersecurity Dataset Observatory: Which Data for AI in Cybersecurity?
2257c9d5db5fcc13fc72aa73.excerpt: arXiv:2611.20812v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: AI is increasingly used for cybersecurity tasks such as intrusion and malware detection, in enterprise, industrial, vehicular and mobile networks. Its effectiveness depends on data: models need representative network traffic, both to be trained and to be evaluated realistically. Public datasets of cybersecurity network traffic, however, are scattered across laboratory pages, repositories and aggregators, and are continuously released, corrected and withdrawn: 92 of the 234 datasets we catalog were released in 2023 or later. At this pace, surveys that list them are outdated soon after publication, since they describe the field only as it was when they were written. New datasets are added as they are found or submitted, every record is periodically re-checked against its original source, to which it links rather than hosting the data, and every change is recorded in a public change log. This paper documents the first release: we define a traffic-centered scope and a seven-axis taxonomy, and review 234 datasets (204 original captures and 30 derivatives) across 14 domains. The review shows a field that grows quickly but unevenly, where 91 datasets distribute only processed records, a few laboratories produce a large share of the data, and UAV, wireless and V2X networks have little

ad36de9115f4667af8b538a4.title_original: TUSI: A Citation-Grounded Graph-Based Benchmark for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Persian Legal Question Answering
ad36de9115f4667af8b538a4.excerpt: arXiv:2611.21823v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Evaluating retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems in Persian law remains challenging because benchmarks lack realism, grounding, and coverage of legal reasoning. To address this gap, we introduce TUSI-Bench, a structured Persian legal benchmark designed for the evaluation of RAG-based systems. We also construct a legal knowledge graph linking articles and concepts for structure-aware retrieval. Furthermore, we propose a graph-based retrieval baseline that leverages relational structure within the legal knowledge graph. Experimental results

5d42e7eb1b2092cd825c63d6.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22446v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Conventional knowledge distillation can facilitate the propagation of backdoors from teacher models to student models. However, the attack success rate rapidly approaches 100% once a critical threshold is exceeded. Second, backdoor propagation does not depend on explicit malicious responses. 7018199379cef4631f0076ad.title_original: JointGV: Structure-Aware Correction of Visual World Models with Parallel Graph Dynamics for Long-Horizon Modeling
7018199379cef4631f0076ad.excerpt: arXiv:2611.22543v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Visual world models predict future visual states conditioned on actions, but recursive errors in entity poses and spatial relations limit their long-horizon prediction for robot planning and control. 38bf1d5f0fc14b6b96e3dc6b.title_original: PIPETTE: Prompt Injection Purple-Teaming for Robust LLM Agents
38bf1d5f0fc14b6b96e3dc6b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.24362v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents routinely interact with untrusted external data, exposing them to indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks that hijack agents into executing attacker-chosen tasks. To address this gap, we introduce PIPETTE, a unified prompt injection purple-teaming framework that effectively converts red-teaming discoveries into defender robustness improvements. b672444ab2a0214060468420.title_original: Hypnos: A Dual-Phase End-to-End Platform for Scalable Continual Learning at the Edge
b672444ab2a0214060468420.excerpt: arXiv:2611.24637v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Continual learning (CL) enables neural networks to adapt to non-stationary data streams by mitigating catastrophic forgetting, offering a path to robust, private, and adaptable edge devices. cb82ba4eb201700ac1d3392c.excerpt: arXiv:2611.24782v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Neural networks trained on the same task develop related weight-space structures, yet remain distinguishable after learning. Final weights thus retain selective historical information rather than a complete trajectory record. 17c5404f163b527eff900e77.title_original: TipDex-VTLA: Learning to Refine Actions with Visual Reliability and Tactile Feedback for Dexterous Manipulation
17c5404f163b527eff900e77.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25683v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Changes in illumination can induce action drift in dexterous manipulation even when the physical state remains unchanged. Specifically, Visual Action Sensitivity Estimation (VASE) learns visual reliability from a frozen reference policy's action sensitivity to illumination perturbations. This effectively helps to refine actions under challenging unseen visual conditions. We evaluate TipDex-VTLA on four real-world dexterous manipulation tasks and the UniVTAC simulation benchmark. TipDex-VTLA trained on data collected under normal visual conditions, achieves average full-task success rates of 87.5% (resp. 73.8%) under normal (resp. challenging unseen) lighting in real-world tasks, significantly outperforming some state-of-the-art methods. We will release the collected data and source code.

f6bb4c927f45dddb9ed69c55.title_original: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models
f6bb4c927f45dddb9ed69c55.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25927v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Latent world models predict the outcomes of action sequences, but comparing candidate plans through recursive rollout remains expensive at test time. We introduce Fast-JEPA, a latent world model planning framework that advances the success-latency Pareto frontier of predictive search. Fast-JEPA reorganizes predictive computation to support effective action-sequence search at low planning cost. It constructs a goal-directed plan to guide search and directly predicts the outcomes of complete candidates for efficient comparison, avoiding recursive state rollout during refinement. Across PushT, Reacher, Cube, and TwoRoom, Fast-JEPA achieves 96.50% average success rate with 2.41x faster planning than INTACT. Search-budget sweeps show that its competitive success and low latency extend across candidate counts and refinement depths. We further introduce DynaGoal, a benchmark for evaluating world-model planning under dynamic out-of-distribution conditions, execution deadlines, and controlled response delays. Fast-JEPA achieves average success rates of 73.83% on DynaGoal-Shift and 87.67% on DynaGoal-Deadline, demonstrating the practical value of low-latency predictive planning under changing control conditions and execution-time constraints. Our project page is available at https://deepcybo-physai.github.io/Fast-JEPA.

0f811fdbd38eb1d33ce4ad82.title_original: C-LiTE: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Cellular feature learning in Histopathology
0f811fdbd38eb1d33ce4ad82.excerpt: arXiv:2611.26316v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Characterising individual cells is fundamental to computational pathology, as cellular morphology informs tasks such as tumour grading, mitotic assessment and immune profiling. We further assemble a pre-training dataset of 60 million cell-centred crops from TCGA, balanced across 19 cancer types and 16 tissu

0a7bf1b89799faf1a04faba6.title_original: Development of an Effective Federated Learning-Based Defense System Against Phishing Attacks on Mobile Platforms
0a7bf1b89799faf1a04faba6.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phishing remains one of the most pervasive and damaging cyber threats, exploiting both technical flaws and human behavior to compromise sensitive data. We present a privacy-preserving, real-time defense that analyzes full webpage source code on mobile platforms. Our system combines a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for end-to-end feature extraction with a Federated Learning (FL) framework that updates models collaboratively on user devices without transferring raw data-supporting regulatory compliance and personalization. We further demonstrate an end-to-end integration within the open-source Lightning Android browser, achieving real-time detection with low computational overhead. This work shows that privacy-first, AI-driven phishing detection is both feasible and scalable across mobile and IoT settings, delivering robust protection while keeping user data on-device.

7e113185b6052547eab14e8a.title_original: An LLM-Assisted Multi-Objective AutoML Framework for Efficient Network Intrusion Detection
7e113185b6052547eab14e8a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional Machine Learning (ML)-based Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) require manual design, optimize only detection performance, and neglect inference latency and model size, which are critical for resource-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) and Electric Vehicle Charging System (EVCS) deployments. 4f4c775991b7583f6ea159ca.title_original: Quantity-Level FDIA in SDR-Based P2P Energy Trading: Cyber-Economic Impact and Pre-Clearing Detection
4f4c775991b7583f6ea159ca.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the cyber-economic impact and pre-clearing detectability of false data injection attacks (FDIAs) in peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading among interconnected microgrids. In the investigated case study, measurable downstream economic distortion and low pre-clearing detectability coexist under bounded

73d8f44dd6cf52339be41880.title_original: Enabling Verifiable Output Lineage for Virtualized ML Workload Execution
73d8f44dd6cf52339be41880.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning (ML) property attestation lets a model provider demonstrate properties of their models and datasets to verifiers, and trusted execution environments (TEEs) have emerged as its most practical mechanism. It binds the execution status to measurements of the operation's inputs and outputs, enabling verifiers to assess run-time behavior through ML property attestation. We implement EVOLVE on Intel TDX as a Rust module within its virtual firmware, with policy checks built on primitives formally verified in F*. Our evaluation shows that EVOLVE is versatile across diverse ML applications on unmodified hardware, provides formal guarantees for its policy checks. EVOLVE incurs per-request run-time

c194924820d7b1a70642ce7a.title_original: Weight-Space Backdoors in Open-Weight LLMs: Cross-Architecture Attacks and Blind Model Forensics
c194924820d7b1a70642ce7a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-weight language models are vulnerable to trigger-conditioned behaviors introduced through sparse post-training weight modifications, creating supply-chain risks beyond conventional provenance checks. cef588493c4f2e94e23d5170.title_original: Praxis: Practical Witness Encryption for NP
cef588493c4f2e94e23d5170.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Witness encryption encrypts a message to an NP statement so that whoever holds a witness can decrypt. c77321ff91f30ade14abeda9.title_original: A Model Obfuscation and Controllable Authorization Scheme for Deep Learning as a Service
c77321ff91f30ade14abeda9.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Developing deep learning models requires substantial computational and data resources, making them core intellectual assets for enterprises. As Deep Learning as a Service (DLaaS) increasingly extends to edge computing environments, models deployed on third-party devices face growing threats from reverse engineering. Existing model protection methods often depend on specialized hardware or incur substantial computational overhead, while lacking effective mechanisms for controlling model usage. There is therefore a need for lightweight solutions that combine model protection with controllable authorization. To address this challenge, we propose KeyObf, a model obfuscation and controllable authorization scheme for DLaaS. KeyObf efficiently protects model parameters and architecture through model obfuscation while binding parameter recovery to user keys, ensuring that only authorized users can perform inference correctly. By integrating a key-based mechanism into the obfuscation framework, KeyObf unifies model protection and controllable authorization. Experimental results demonstrate that KeyObf preserves the inference accuracy of authorized users, rejects inference requests when credential authentication fails, and increases the difficulty of recovering model information under the evaluated reverse-engineering conditions. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a lightweight approach to model protection and controllable autho

dbfc270b7384ff4c1ee45030.title_original: Anti OS Fingerprinting, Revisited: A Loadable Kernel Module for FreeBSD and What Twenty-Five Years Changed
dbfc270b7384ff4c1ee45030.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2001 we published a paper on an Anti OS Detection (AoD) system: a modified FreeBSD 4.3 kernel that makes a host answer the probes of an OS fingerprinting tool as if it ran another operating system. This report revisits that work on FreeBSD 15.1. We do not claim a new method. We report three things. First, the same goal is now reachable from a loadable module of about 800 lines that uses the packet filter hook interface and sets one kernel variable, without changing the kernel source. Second, the module covers both active and passive fingerprinting: Nmap 7.98 reports an exact match for Linux and for Windows 10/11, and p0f 3 reports the same systems from the connections the host opens. Third, an exact match in Nmap was not enough: a passive tool, plain FIN scans and a comparison with real hosts each exposed a mismatch that the previous step could not see. A real Windows 11 host and the final Windows personality get the same verdict from Nmap and the same signatures from p0f and JA4T; a real Linux 7.0 host is not an exact match in Nmap at all, while the personality built from Nmap's database is. We describe those mismatches, how we removed them, what the module costs, and what it still cannot hide.

f618d351ff54fe083d023484.title_original: InstantCoFFEA: Fast and accurate Tor flow correlation at realistic scale
f618d351ff54fe083d023484.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tor end-to-end correlation attacks can link a client to its destination by matching traffic observed at both ends of a Tor circuit. However, their practical threat remains unclear for two reasons: existing correlation methods rely on O(N^2) pairwise processing, and prior works do not reflect the flow counts and base rates seen by realistic adversaries. We present InstantCoFFEA, which replaces exhaustive pairwise search with approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) retrieval using CAGRA and introduces ranked voting. At N = 200k, InstantCoFFEA is 14.56x faster than DeepCoFFEA and improves PR-AUC from 0.94 to 0.96. We also use TorPS to estimate the flow counts and matching-pair base rates observed by relay-level and network-level adversaries. Our simulations show that realistic attacks involve substantially more candidate flows and much lower base rates than those used in prior evaluations. Under a low-base-rate setting, PR-AUC drops for all methods, but InstantCoFFEA achieves 0.53 compared with 0.42 for DeepCoFFEA. These results show that evaluating correlation attacks requires considering both computational scale and the sparsity of true matching pairs.

98452092f4c7b504f7e80bb2.title_original: QUISA: A Compact, Flexible and Unified Instruction-Set Coprocessor for QR-UOV Signature
98452092f4c7b504f7e80bb2.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: QR-UOV is a Quotient Ring Unbalanced Oil and Vinegar (UOV) multivariate quadratic (MQ) signature scheme that has progressed to round-3 of the post-quantum cryptography (PQC) additional signatures call by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). To minimize hardware resources, we propose a modular arithmetic unit with finite-field reduction based on the shift-add folding method. The design introduces a linear system solver for QUISA based on LU decomposition with partial pivoting and a sample solution module, operating over the prime field Fq (q = 127). 5ae16873d6dc090132faf201.title_original: Who Is Prompt-Injecting Coding Agents? An Empirical Study of Hidden AI-Directed Text on GitHub
5ae16873d6dc090132faf201.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI coding agents now triage issues, review pull requests and pick up tasks inside GitHub repositories, and to do so they read text that anyone with a GitHub account can write. We analyzed roughly 145 million issues, pull requests, comments and README files, detected text that GitHub does not render to a human reader but that an agent receives in full, and filtered it with a two-stage LLM classification, a template provenance check and an exhaustive manual review. We identify 2,281 validated findings in issues, pull requests and comments (16 per million items), and AI-directed hidden text in the READMEs of 107 repositories. We find a heterogeneous ecosystem of four uses: attacks on other parties' agents, defensive text that restricts agents, content override that steers what they write, and first-party orchestration, in which projects coordinate their own agents through hidden markers. 31238c4cb844bfcf46be4ddf.title_original: More Is Never Less: Affordable Robustness to Additive Attacks via Monotone Multiple-Instance Learning
31238c4cb844bfcf46be4ddf.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Static malware detectors that represent each sample as a bag of extracted features, such as permissions, API calls, or imported functions, are cheap to deploy and remain state-of-the-art under temporal drift and in selective classification. To this end, we propose MalSets, which uses max-pooled Deep Sets models with a monotone head to ensure that any malicious evidence remains undiluted; thus, more is never less. Under MIL, a general text encoder maps any feature string to an embedding, thus eliminating the long-standing out-of-vocabulary problem at test time. Max-pooling retains the malicious evidence regardless of how many benign features an attacker adds. c2a754bc4360d34203287835.title_original: Ads for Agents: Measuring Ad-Serving MCP Servers
c2a754bc4360d34203287835.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents call external tools through protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Some MCP servers return paid advertisements (ads) into the model's context. The model then decides whether these ads and their disclosures reach the user. We trace these ads from their sources to the agent's tool results across public MCP servers and packages. We find the servers through their public traces in ad networks, package registries, certificate logs, hostnames, MCP directories, and GitHub configurations. We then query the ad-serving servers with read-only requests and inspect their ad links. Ads appear on only 0.57% of 101,363 open MCP endpoints and 0.04% of 122,656 local MCP packages. Although 173 ad networks target agents, operators insert the ads themselves on about half of the 226 ad-returning servers. Nearly all ad-serving packages likewise carry the operator's own affiliate identifier. While ads adapt to the topic and intent of the query, their disclosure stays fixed within each tool. Only 9.3% of the ads carry an explicit sponsored label. Most ad links also hide their destinations. Since operators insert most ads themselves and label them inconsistently, we propose a per-item ad annotation in MCP results. Clients can show this annotation to the user independently of the model's answer.

8657a3a1a23b92bda4e41fa4.title_original: Intrinsic Value Modules: Trusted-Hardware Support for Locally Final Offline Asset Transfer
8657a3a1a23b92bda4e41fa4.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consensus lets distributed participants agree on a common state, but it makes monetary validity depend on network connectivity and collective acceptance. We explore making validity intrinsic to a digital coin. We propose an \emph{Intrinsic Value Module (IVM)}: trusted hardware that gives a coin locally verifiable authenticity and spendability, analogous to verifying a signature. Under stated hardware and cryptographic assumptions, the IVM abstraction and our offline transfer protocol move monetary uniqueness from a replicated ledger into non-clonable protected state. The protocol prevents forgery, replay, double credit, and double spending by genuine, uncompromised IVMs; communication failures may lock value but cannot duplicate it. We distinguish local transfer atomicity and asset uniqueness, which the protocol establishes, from global state consistency across disconnected devices, which it does not. The IVM does not eliminate trust; it relocates trust to certified hardware, issuer roots, and non-rollback state. We present the architecture, protocol, and security analysis, and discuss open challenges.

e020e3f18e7a06d3f2d148d5.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Confidential GPUs offer near-native on-device compute performance, but transfers between CPU and GPU TEEs through untrusted host memory require bulk CPU encryption and decryption, even for unchanged data. Reusing exported ciphertext could avoid this work, but GPU TEE firmware enforces direction-specific encryption keys and fresh per-transfer initialization vectors (IVs), preventing direct reuse. With this modification, GPU's subsequent read on the retained ciphertext can still proceed through the GPU's hardware-fixed copy-engine interfaces, which cannot be modified by software. An additional GPU correction step can then compensate for differences in the keys and IVs to recover the original plaintext. cbf1432fc5c16e4403413897.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety alignment is widely used to align large language models (LLMs) to produce helpful and harmless responses. However, an attacker can plant a jailbreak backdoor in an LLM such that adding a universal trigger word or phrase to a harmful prompt elicits attacker-desired responses. Existing jailbreak backdoor attacks induce distinct behaviors on backdoored inputs and safety samples (harmful prompts paired with refusal responses), making the backdoors susceptible to subsequent safety alignment and advanced defenses. In this paper, we propose a persistent jailbreak backdoor attack that reduces the divergence between clean and trigger-conditioned continuations during LLM decoding, making backdoored samples difficult to distinguish from safety samples. We also introduce a deferred-response mechanism that postpones harmful generations, further disguising the backdoor behavior. We evaluate our attack, PJBack, on eight LLMs from five model families, ranging from 7B to 70B parameters. PJBack achieves an average attack success rate of 93.9% and bypasses all seven evaluated defenses while preserving benign utility. In contrast, five existing backdoor attacks either achieve limited attack success or fail to withstand the evaluated defenses.

c11e0960a516aedac8b803e1.title_original: TurboFHE: An Efficient and Scalable Multi-GPU Framework for Homomorphic LLM Inference

Its compiler can split different nodes of the same computation graph at the ciphertext and polynomial level. Guided by a measurement-based performance model, its hardware-aware planner jointly optimizes task partitioning, placement, operand residency, and transfer scheduling. %Critical-path-guided rewrites extract shared computation and restructure homomorphic sums. Its backend then generates optimized GPU kernels and executes plans using CUDA graphs and selective point-to-point transfers. \fwName adapts its plans to diverse hardware configurations and FHE inference algorithms for large-scale models. On A100 GPUs, \fwName achieves $98.0\%$, $91.8\%$, and $79.3\%$ parallel efficiency for the same workload on 2, 4, and 8 GPUs, respectively.

7a81aafb2487ae859fbe173b.title_original: Revealing Semantic Gaps in Zero-Knowledge Virtual Machines via Obligation-Targeted Semantic Fuzzing
7a81aafb2487ae859fbe173b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zero-knowledge virtual machines (zkVMs) prove correct execution of programs and underpin systems securing billions of dollars in digital assets. Mismatches, or semantic gaps, come in two kinds: underconstraint bugs let a malicious prover forge a proof of an execution the ISA forbids (a soundness violation), and divergence bugs make the zkVM itself deviate from the ISA or crash, so an honest prover cannot prove a legitimate execution (a completeness violation). Both cluster at corner cases such as division by zero that conventional fuzzing almost never reaches, and underconstraint bugs leave program output unchanged. Our key insight is that these corner cases correspond to constraint obligations derived from the ISA specification and the proof system's algebraic structure. We build Beak, a reinforcement-learning fuzzer in which obligations replace three random decisions: they supply inputs that trigger each obligation, reward executions that trigger new combinations of obligations, and direct witness tampering to the step where an obligation is triggered. 1547afd9193ba50914b8ca40.title_original: Benchmarking Web Agent Defenses Against Adaptive Visual Prompt Injection
1547afd9193ba50914b8ca40.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal web agents automate website interactions but remain vulnerable to visual prompt injection (VPI), where malicious webpage content manipulates their visual processing and induces unintended actions. We also introduce three metrics to measure the extent of agent hijacking at three different levels. Across 10 defense configurations for computer-use agents and 11 defense configurations for browser-use agents, our adaptive attacks achieve average success rates of 91.87% and 91.99%, respectively. d0fa24c276b54b03e8515908.title_original: AscendFHE: Efficient Fully Homomorphic Encryption on Ascend NPUs
d0fa24c276b54b03e8515908.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption enables cloud servers to run neural networks on encrypted inputs. In CKKS, inference requires costly arithmetic on high-degree polynomials. On Ascend neural processing units, preparing operands and reconstructing intermediate results add to this cost, while limited local memory constrains parallel execution. We present AscendFHE, a CKKS backend that coordinates Ascend's matrix engines and vector cores for bootstrapping and encrypted inference. It uses balanced-byte encoding and exact modular reconstruction to reduce vector work and packs intermediate results in the next operator's input format to avoid redundant transfers. Its two-task pipeline reuses shared buffers after their last read to overlap matrix and vector execution within the local memory budget. On Ascend 910B3, AscendFHE achieves a 4.61$\times$ bootstrapping speedup and 1.59$\times$--2.00$\times$ encrypted-inference speedups across ResNet-20, BERT-base, and Llama 3 8B over our Vector-based Ascend port of Cheddar.

f64bcc8e87a687e54ebee765.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complex packing in CKKS stores two real streams in the real and imaginary lanes of each slot. It reuses dual-lane squares in polynomial activations and the modular-reduction stage of CKKS bootstrapping. 13cc32bb9ee544750122cc05.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables computation directly on encrypted data, but its substantial computational cost hinders adoption in privacy-preserving artificial intelligence (AI) applications. cd640b5aa8c8f38b28ca226d.title_original: NRSnooper: Enabling Real-Time Bidirectional Traffic Decoding in Commercial 5G NR Networks
cd640b5aa8c8f38b28ca226d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decoding both uplink and downlink cellular traffic reveals lower-layer protocol behavior, unprotected signaling, and encrypted higher-layer packets beyond what scheduling metadata exposes. We present NRSnooper, a passive sniffer that decodes downlink control and bidirectional data traffic in real time, including traffic from already-connected UEs and traffic after encrypted configuration updates. NRSnooper learns reusable physical-layer configurations through an instrumented open-source UE that reproduces commercial UE capabilities. It recovers connection-specific identifiers from ongoing transmissions and selects matching configurations through CRC-validated data decoding. A hybrid CPU-GPU pipeline sustains continuous wideband processing. Evaluations on a controlled testbed and two commercial networks show that, compared with using only configurations from unencrypted signaling, NRSnooper decodes 1.3x and 6.3x as many control messages and 9.0x and 17.7x as many downlink data blocks, respectively. d09a2d028fa3160b2dde01d6.title_original: Mitigating Nested GTP Attacks: A Closed-Loop eBPF Defense for 5G and Beyond Networks
d09a2d028fa3160b2dde01d6.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The evolving cellular networks continue to rely on the legacy GPRS Tunneling Protocol-User Plane (GTP-U) to encapsulate and route user data traffic across the data plane. 1f291d17a93d33734d1f6dd8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Commercial AI agents increasingly incorporate long-term memory (both persistent and chat-history) to enable more accurate and personalized responses, raises significant privacy and policy concerns. LODESTONE combines text cross-encoder and directed-graph relevance scores to extract compact alert-centered subgraphs, retrieves article-level knowledge graphs through node- and edge-level dual-softmax assignment, and uses a fine-tuned 4B-parameter LLM to align event combinations with CTI attack steps. fdb10ee850b5d296107fba6d.title_original: Packing Stern into L2: GPU-Accelerated Primal-Shortened ISD for High-Codimension Binary Goppa Key Recovery
fdb10ee850b5d296107fba6d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Primal-Shortened Information-Set Decoding (ISD) with quadratic polar lifting recently pushed TII McEliece Track-2 key recovery to $mt=126$ (TII-228, $2{,}463$ CPU core-hours), with over $99\%$ of runtime spent harvesting weight-$(2t+1)$ codewords. Porting MiniMax's Mode-6 Stern sampler directly to one block per SM leaves $1.0\text{-}1.5\text{ GB}$ of hash tables active and stalls on global memory. For $mt \le 145$, we pack all $mt-17 \le 128$ remaining syndrome bits into one $16$-byte ulonglong2 without left-triple indices, share $G \in \{4, 8\}$ cooperative tables inside GPU L2 cache, batch $64G$ random systematic reductions per launch, and widen the shortening prefix $n'$ to cut modeled GPU-hours by $34\%\text{-}47\%$. Across four Track-2 challenges ($mt = 108 \to 144$), every recovered private key passes both the official SageMath checker and a standalone pure-Python verifier. Eight Modal L40S GPUs solve TII-228 ($mt=126$) in $18.9\text{ min}$ ($2.15$ GPU-hours, $3.0\times$ faster in wall-clock than MiniMax's EPYC cluster). We further recover keys for the previously undocumented challenges TII-237 ($mt=135$, $22.1$ L4 GPU-hours) and TII-235 ($mt=144$, $4.30\text{ h}$ across ten L40S GPUs, $39.62$ GPU-hours, $17.97\text{ s}$ lift), using $127$ of $128$ packed bits. These results do not demonstrate practical recovery against Classic McEliece parameters ($mt \ge 768$).

6dd0c822dec13d40b00ea142.title_original: IDSMorph: Self-Adaptive Malicious Traffic Detection through Consistency-Guided Dynamic Decision Boundaries
6dd0c822dec13d40b00ea142.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anomaly-based malicious traffic detection learns decision boundaries for normal behavior and identifies deviations as anomalies. However, normal behavior varies across networks and changes dynamically, limiting adaptability and increasing retraining costs. Despite this variability, our measurements show that clients accessing the same service exhibit consistent flow structures and interaction patterns, since each service provides specific functionality. We therefore construct service-specific decision boundaries. However, variations in personalized requests make it difficult to construct stable boundaries. To address this challenge, we propose IDSMorph, a self-adaptive malicious traffic detection system that learns consistency-guided embeddings through two key designs: (1) a flow structure consistency builder, which constructs contrastive samples capturing consistent embeddings within services; and (2) a service interaction consistency builder, which captures local structural consistency among different clients and global behavioral consistency among clients accessing that service. IDSMorph constructs dynamic decision boundaries from the majority of similar embeddings within each service and dynamically updates them through a differencing algorithm that mitigates the transient traffic shifts within short observation windows. Experiments show that IDSMorph's detection F1 score decreases by no more than 0.12 points across network

e7c4ea448cc72fc878bd32b4.title_original: EnvTrap: Revealing the Environment-Only Attack Surface in Embodied AI via Consequence-Blind Action Execution
e7c4ea448cc72fc878bd32b4.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI models evolve from text and vision to physical agents, embodied AI faces a fundamentally different attack surface. Prior attacks on embodied systems have used crafted instructions, adversarial visual inputs, and training-time policy modifications; we study environment-only object rearrangements with unchanged models and instructions. We reveal an attack surface in safety-critical spatial relations among existing objects. An adversary who rearranges objects, without modifying instructions or accessing models, can cause hazardous consequences. In this work, we propose EnvTrap, a diagnostic pipeline that constructs paired safe, trap, and null-trap (benign but misleading) embodied scenarios. We demonstrate that environment-only perturbations raise hazardous-action rates to an average of 83.4% across the five evaluated action policies, with similar vulnerability patterns confirmed in world models. On a consequence-prediction task, model accuracy remains near chance, while human evaluators achieve high accuracy. We further propose a consequence-aware defense that reduces trap trigger rates by an average of 76.3 percentage points across action policies in simulation and by 62.9 percentage points pooled across physical backends. b756827a18f11e51dc0e31ba.title_original: LaTSEC: Lattice-Based Threshold Signatures with Native Non-Interactive Identifiable Abort and Compact Per-Party Storage
b756827a18f11e51dc0e31ba.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present $\mathsf{LaTSEC}$, a three-round lattice-based threshold signature scheme with native non-interactive identifiable abort. Each party holds one small-norm signing share and is associated with one public abort key, against which its partial signature is verified directly, without zero-knowledge proofs or an additional interactive protocol. Prior lattice-based threshold signatures that identify misbehaving parties rely on one of three mechanisms: zero-knowledge proofs, an additional interactive protocol, or an everywhere-short secret sharing scheme in which each party holds multiple signing shares, each with its own public abort key. Compared with schemes that use the third mechanism, $\mathsf{LaTSEC}$ substantially reduces per-party storage. The construction uses $\mathsf{SEC}$, a recent ramp everywhere-short secret sharing scheme based on lossless expanders that gives each party a single short share. We prove correctness, identifiable-abort security, and threshold unforgeability under the standard $\mathsf{MLWE}$ and $\mathsf{MSIS}$ assumptions. The unforgeability proof introduces the Repeated-$\boldsymbol{A}$ Matrix Hint-MLWE problem, a new variant of $\mathsf{MLWE}$ with hints that captures the complete tuple of correlated public abort keys. 3ad6111ff7a3f1972fef17fd.title_original: Quantum-Resilient, PUF-Based, and Anonymity-Preserving Authentication and Key Agreement Scheme for UAV Networks
3ad6111ff7a3f1972fef17fd.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We design a lightweight authentication and key agreement protocol for Internet of Drones (IoD) environments that simultaneously provides post-quantum security, hardware-rooted trust, and resistance against machine-learning-based Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) modeling attacks. Existing PUF-based authentication schemes for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) offer protection against cloning and physical capture, but generally lack resistance against quantum adversaries. Conversely, recent post-quantum UAV authentication protocols provide quantum-resistant key establishment, yet do not incorporate hardware-bound authentication mechanisms and therefore remain vulnerable to device cloning and physical compromise. To address these limitations, we integrate CRYSTALS-Kyber, dynamic challenge scrambling (DCS), fuzzy extractors, and PUF-based identity binding into a unified framework. The resulting protocol enables anonymous authentication, forward secrecy, resistance to physical capture and replay attacks, and secure drone-to-drone communication, while maintaining suitability for resource-constrained UAV platforms. We provide a formal security analysis of the proposed scheme under the real-or-random model, a ProVerif-based formal verification, an informal analysis of its effectiveness against various attacks, and a performance evaluation of the proposed scheme through communication, computation, and storage cost analyses, which show its

93e7c0e8e609ceae580f6f31.title_original: CHIP: Contrastive Hardware-Image Projection. Can OpenAI CLIP Reconstruct Images from the CPU Computational Footprint?
93e7c0e8e609ceae580f6f31.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Image inference on a shared CPU leaves input-dependent traces in software-visible performance counters and execution time. CHIP (Contrastive Hardware-Image Projection) trains a lightweight residual projector on public images to map these measurements into the 768-dimensional visual embedding space of a frozen OpenAI CLIP model. A frozen Stable unCLIP generator uses the projected embeddings to reconstruct recognizable color scenes for held-out inputs. The attack requires no physical probe, candidate image gallery, domain-specific generator, or shared cache, and elapsed time alone retains the signal. We evaluate full-counter, single-counter, and timing-only measurements on Intel Haswell and Sapphire Rapids. The projected embeddings achieve 0.85 ROC AUC for held-out image identification, compared with a 0.50 baseline. Exact-image top-five retrieval reaches 24% on CIFAR-100 and 56% on Unsafe-Diffusion. Across both processors, reconstructions average $1.4\times$ the baseline RGB color-palette overlap and $2.5\times$ the baseline structural similarity.

3424d24ca7fa34b0b60cf2e1.title_original: MirrorGuard: Defending LiDAR Perception against Passive Mirror Attacks
3424d24ca7fa34b0b60cf2e1.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mirror-based LiDAR attacks passively redirect automotive LiDAR's beams to create phantom objects in the vehicle perception. Recent work has demonstrated that these attacks may cause vehicles to brake for a phantom where nothing stands. Every phantom return is a genuine time-of-flight measurement, so current spoofing defenses are not able to differentiate phantoms from real objects. We present MirrorGuard, a physics-informed defense that identifies and removes mirror-induced phantom returns before they affect downstream perception. MirrorGuard tests three consequences of the reflected path. Every phantom bearing crosses the mirror's finite aperture, its opaque surface blocks any direct return beyond it, and the two reflections off the mirror dim the phantom. MirrorGuard identifies a phantom by these cues over multiple scans and removes the reflected beams before it reaches any detector or occupancy grid. On real-world recordings of this attack, MirrorGuard removes 96.31% of the phantom's returns at 98.30% precision, with 99.99% of non-phantom returns untouched. In a closed loop with the CARLA driving simulator and the open-source stack (Autoware), a vehicle without the defense halts for an obstacle that is not present and a following car crashes into its rear. With MirrorGuard, no vehicle produces a halt or a crash. MirrorGuard runs at 59 ms mean per scan on a CPU and is a software-only solution that does not require new hardware

983b7c14e5337df9a2977564.title_original: AutoClip-DPZO: Practical Private Clipping Selection for Differentially Private Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning
983b7c14e5337df9a2977564.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Differentially private zeroth-order optimization (DPZO) is a promising approach for privacy-preserving LLM fine-tuning, offering exceptional memory efficiency. However, its utility is highly sensitive to the clipping threshold $C$, a key DP-specific hyperparameter that controls the trade-off between noise injection and clipping bias. Existing DPZO methods typically tune $C$ by repeatedly evaluating candidate values and reporting the best result, which is computationally expensive and incurs additional privacy cost that must be accounted for under DP. Designing a practical DP procedure for selecting $C$ in DPZO is challenging because no fixed choice performs well across settings, straightforward search-based strategies suffer from poor utility and efficiency, and existing clipping-selection methods for DPSGD do not transfer well to DPZO due to its fundamentally different error regime. In this paper, we propose AutoClip-DPZO, a practical DP method that automatically and efficiently selects $C$ for DPZO. Our key idea is to avoid fine-tuning-based search by reducing clipping selection to a private quantile estimation problem, where the target quantile depends only on public privacy and training parameters. To derive this selection rule, we develop a novel characterization of DPZO error as a function of $C$ that captures both noise variance and clipping bias while remaining accurate and easy to optimize. 47268c9c88c1af5201e8104b.title_original: ArguShield: Enforcing Minimum-Necessary Disclosure in Tool-Calling LLM Agents
47268c9c88c1af5201e8104b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents increasingly use third-party tools to complete user tasks. Even without malicious intent, they may fill broad or weakly constrained fields with private information that is unnecessary or inappropriate for the receiving tool. Such calls can satisfy the tool schema and complete the task, yet still violate minimum-necessary disclosure. We introduce ArguShield, a mediation layer that intercepts proposed tool calls before execution. It evaluates each candidate value using three signals: Value Provenance, Task Relevance, and Disclosure Boundary. ArguShield releases justified values, defers values that need user confirmation, and withholds those outside the permitted scope. We evaluate ArguShield with four tool-calling models on ArgPrivBench, a benchmark of 120 tasks across Travel, Shopping, and Healthcare. Unprotected agents frequently over-disclose private information despite high task success. Prompt-only protection reduces unauthorized disclosure but substantially lowers task success. ArguShield reduces unauthorized silent release to 9% on Standard tasks and 6% on High-risk tasks while preserving recoverable task success under simulated user confirmation.

7f8387b1d8339367c027eae5.title_original: Bounded Autonomy: A Trust-Anchored Defense Against Resource-Exhaustion Attacks on Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
7f8387b1d8339367c027eae5.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-augmented Large Language Model (LLM) agents are vulnerable to resource-exhaustion attacks that amplify model-token consumption through persistent context amplification, large tool output amplification, and error-induced agentic loops. Despite growing attention to agent security and resource-abuse risks, a systematic defense framework specifically targeting these attacks remains lacking. Meanwhile, existing general-purpose agent defense frameworks, which address a broader range of security threats, often rely on prompt-level safeguards or coarse-grained resource limits and lack deterministic runtime mechanisms for controlling token consumption. They also provide limited support for balancing fault recovery against the risk of repeated resource-consuming execution. To address these limitations, we propose a trust-anchored closed-loop defense framework consisting of four phases: certificate-guided orchestration with deterministic handoffs, calibrated one-time node budgeting, Gateway-based runtime enforcement, and bounded recovery through a shared, non-resettable recovery pool. By accounting for both input and output tokens across all model invocations, our experiments demonstrate that the framework bounds cumulative token consumption, mitigates resource-amplification attacks, and preserves benign task utility under trusted execution assumptions.

14529200eb0ea4b8fb5bb6be.title_original: WEPWAWET-CORE: A Hardware-Resident ML-DSA Architecture with Fabric-Generated, Fabric-Sealed Keys for Post-Quantum Avionics
14529200eb0ea4b8fb5bb6be.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spacecraft that exchange commands over crosslinks need quantum-resistant signatures, for which the Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA, FIPS 204) is the standard, yet a software signer runs its data-dependent rejection loop, and keeps its key, on cores and memory shared with attitude control and payload processing. This paper shows that for a hardware-assisted signer the cost that matters is not the arithmetic but the number of times the processor crosses into the fabric, and that the boundary which minimizes those crossings is also where the key can be sealed. A gem5-supported analysis of three control granularities over the same kernels shows that only one job per signature, with the whole rejection loop on chip, takes the processor off the critical path. WEPWAWET-CORE realizes that boundary on an XCZU3EG at 300 MHz: a ROM microsequencer runs Sign, Verify, and key generation as three programs over one datapath and a banked scratchpad, and keeps the key, the on-die entropy, and the mask seed off the processor bus. The processor-side cost of a signature falls from over a second under per-kernel control to 0.53 ms, fixed whatever the number of rejections, and the fabric's time per attempt varies by less than 0.1% under a saturating workload. e801bf0dceec64bf48f4415b.title_original: PLATRS: A Lattice-Based Linkable Accountable Ring Signature for Permissioned Blockchains
e801bf0dceec64bf48f4415b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Permissioned-ledger cross-domain data sharing needs anonymity and accountability: an endorsement hides its author, but a regulator must identify it on authorization reuse. Existing lattice-based schemes give these only separately: public traceability exposes signers to collision detectors; linkable non-tracing schemes cannot open; threshold schemes solve another problem. None gives post-quantum security, a signer-chosen ring, a publicly comparable per-event tag, and one-authority opening together. We propose \textsf{PLATRS}, a module-lattice linkable accountable ring signature for permissioned blockchains. Consortium-CA enrollment binds the key returned by an opening to a registered identity. The signer chooses the ring; verification is index-free; each signature has a per-event tag any verifier can compare. Tag noise derives from the signer's tracing secret and event, so linking is one comparison for honest signatures while the tag remains M-LWE without the secret. Detection is two-tier: tag mismatch is immediate; different tags on two accepted signatures for one event trigger an opening; the authority publishes the recovered public opening component, and any member recomputes the verdict against the ring. We prove CPA anonymity from M-LWE, linkability, authority-only traceability, and unforgeability from M-SIS with M-LWE in the random oracle model. b404fb162c69d926821c006f.title_original: From Dependent Ciphertexts to Sharp Bounds for Polynomial Evaluation in BGV
b404fb162c69d926821c006f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central challenge in Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is the selection of ciphertext moduli, which depends on accurately estimating noise growth during homomorphic evaluation. Choosing excessively large moduli reduces the efficiency and scalability of the scheme, whereas underestimating noise can result in decryption failures and potential security vulnerabilities. Average-case analyses have provided promising probabilistic estimates of noise growth in practical FHE computations. However, recent studies indicate that reliable estimates must account for dependencies among ciphertext errors, as neglecting these correlations can systematically underestimate noise. This work presents the first average-case analysis for the BGV scheme that accounts for both correlations induced by secret/public keys and ciphertext dependencies. We propose new variance estimates for the noise coefficients in homomorphic additions and multiplications involving dependent ciphertexts, and extend our framework to the homomorphic evaluation of polynomial functions, which is widely employed in FHE applications. Our theoretical estimates closely align with experimental observations, exhibiting discrepancies smaller than 1.2 bits. a8549b18e33f77d6dea7f0dc.title_original: POMA: Beyond Final Flags -- Process-Level Evaluation of Base LLMs in Vulnerability Exploitation
a8549b18e33f77d6dea7f0dc.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) evolve from text generation to autonomous software-engineering execution, automated vulnerability exploitability verification has emerged as a vital frontier in software quality assurance and security validation. Existing security benchmarks, however, largely judge models by binary pass/fail outcomes or coarse stage milestones. Such outcome-centric scoring obscures fine-grained failure dynamics across long-horizon execution and conflates the intrinsic capability of a base LLM with external agent scaffolding. We present POMA (Pwn-Oriented Model Assessment), a process-level evaluation methodology and platform that isolates base LLMs under a unified execution baseline -- fixing task inputs, tool interfaces, target environments, feedback formats, and execution budgets -- while measuring intermediate states and transitions from runtime evidence. Evaluating four frontier base LLMs across 55 CTF Pwn challenges and 10 real-world vulnerability reproduction tasks exposes persistent capability attrition along the exploitation chain: from vulnerability knowledge to executable implementation, from client-side actions to verified target states, from failure localization to precise repair, and across iterative revisions. In real-world software, models further struggle to satisfy format, semantic, differential, and crash-identity constraints simultaneously. By pinpointing where execution chains break down, POMA p

63cb8071058f4ad9bc58e23f.title_original: Bug Bounty Programs in the AI Era: How Does Platform Anti-Spam Friction Affect Vendor Profitability?
63cb8071058f4ad9bc58e23f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Since 2023, bug bounty platforms have introduced participation rules, such as proof-of-concept mandates, against a flood of AI-generated low-quality submissions. The platforms set these rules, but vendors running programs on them bear the cost when a vulnerability goes unreported and gets exploited. We ask whether the rules benefit the vendors they are meant to protect. Adding to Gal-Or, Hydari, and Telang's 2024 model a vendor triage cost per report reviewed and a participation cost paid in effort by the researchers reporting vulnerabilities, we locate a threshold in an effective triage-burden parameter, which captures the vendor's processing burden per unit of aggregate search effort, with the rules lowering profit below it and raising it above. Because attackers never use the platform, the participation cost falls on researchers alone and fewer take part. Bug-finding coverage falls and breach damage rises, which costs the vendor, while its triage bill falls, which helps.

b7aa9dc16c4157c0fe21c81c.title_original: AgentBouncer: Defending Software Engineering Agents via Dynamic System-Call Mediation
b7aa9dc16c4157c0fe21c81c.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Software engineering (SE) agents can complete diverse engineering tasks by interacting with the development environment via tools that access files, run commands, and download resources. Unfortunately, the same ability that makes SE agents useful also makes them prone to performing unintended malicious actions through prompt injections, malicious tools, or supply-chain attacks. Existing defenses that analyze the agent trajectory may fail to detect such attacks, as they inspect only the initial prompt and the sequence of tool calls, but not the actual actions that are executed in the environment. This paper presents AgentBouncer, a novel runtime enforcement system that prevents SE agents from performing malicious actions by mediating, and if necessary denying, system calls that agents trigger via tool calls. The core of AgentBouncer is an LLM arbiter that judges system calls along two axes, necessity and safety for the current task. It denies unsafe system calls, and the less necessary a system call appears, the more certain the arbiter has to be about its safety to allow it. To manage runtime overhead, preseeded policy rules and hierarchy-aware caching ensure that the LLM arbiter is only invoked for key decisions. We evaluate AgentBouncer on a dataset of 340 attacks on the development environment, covering four attack vectors, combined with benign issue resolution tasks from SWE-bench Verified. c2372879820d8eb609d1e857.title_original: Complying with Cybersecurity Legislation: NIS2 Challenges and Industry Case Study
c2372879820d8eb609d1e857.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given the ever-increasing dependency on interconnected digital systems, cybersecurity has become a major concern. To protect markets and societies, governmental entities are developing legislation to enhance cyber resilience across sectors, introducing new technical and legal requirements. The NIS2 Directive, a revised version of the European-wide cybersecurity legislation, entered into force on 16 January 2023. Member States were required to adopt and publish transposing measures by 17 October 2024 and apply them from 18 October 2024. Specific obligations for essential and important entities are set out in national legislation. At the same time, other organizations, while not legally bound, seek to improve their cybersecurity maturity in alignment with EU-wide advances, for which NIS2 serves as a key reference. This paper presents the work conducted within a large European enterprise to align itself with the NIS2 Directive, focusing on how organizations can analyze and interpret its provisions to drive concrete technical and organizational improvements. A systematic methodology is applied to frame the company within the NIS2 context, identify relevant requirements, and derive actionable measures. Beyond outlining the technical steps taken, the work highlights the challenges of translating legislative requirements into practical implementations, emphasizing the use of existing IT resources while accounting for key legal aspects.

280ae4f561a184786d0f3245.title_original: Demystifying Detectors Guarding Agent Skill Hubs
280ae4f561a184786d0f3245.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent Skills has gained widespread adoption as an open standard for extending agent capabilities. To facilitate skill sharing, public skill hubs have grown in popularity and increasingly rely on automated security detectors to identify malicious skills at scale. Yet, the effectiveness and limitations of these detectors remain insufficiently understood. To fill this gap, we present the first systematic study of four hub-adopted and two community-provided malicious skill detectors on 1477 agent skills from seven datasets. Our evaluation reveals that even the best-performing hub-adopted detector by overall F1, skill-scanner with Qwen3.6, still misses 4.9% of malicious skills and incorrectly flags 17.8% of benign skills. To understand these failures, we manually analyze detectors' findings and decision-making processes, identifying two recurring failure mechanisms. False positives often arise when detectors flag sensitive operations, such as credential access, without considering whether they serve the skill's legitimate purpose. Conversely, false negatives occur when detectors recognize malicious instructions or behaviors but underestimate their severity or dismiss valid findings during review, ultimately leaving malicious skills unblocked. Guided by this analysis, we refine the prompts of a state-of-the-art detector, skill-vetter, improving its mean F1 score in eight of nine evaluation settings, with gains of up to 22.7 percentage

76c62788efc9eef438d488a1.title_original: Carried-Over and Agent-Native Threats in the Supply Chain of LLM Agent Skills
76c62788efc9eef438d488a1.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills are reusable packages that extend a large language model (LLM) agent with scripts, third-party dependencies, and natural-language instructions. An agent builds a skill's arguments from user requests and untrusted external content, so a flaw left by a benign author can escalate a prompt injection to code execution. Existing studies target malicious skills or a single attack vector, and none tests whether an agent can reach such flaws. We present the first registry-scale empirical study of the supply chain attack surface arising from unintentional vulnerabilities in agent skills, over all 48,682 skills in ClawHub. The study covers two carried-over risks, dependencies and first-party code, and two agent-native ones, install instructions and credentials printed to stdout. We screen all skills by static analysis, manually review all 3,428 cases flagged by the four main detectors, and test reachability by running sampled flagged skills in a sandbox and with a live LLM agent under indirect prompt injection. First, dependency risk carries over in a different form: 49.6% of the skills with resolvable dependencies depend on a version with a known CVE, and unlike npm packages, which mostly become vulnerable after release, 78.3% of them are born vulnerable, already exposed at publication.
