3424d24ca7fa34b0b60cf2e1.summary_ko: 연구진은 거울 반사의 물리적 특성으로 차량 LiDAR의 허상 신호를 인지 처리 전에 제거하는 소프트웨어 방어 기법 MirrorGuard를 제안했다. 실제 공격 기록에서 허상 신호 96.31%를 정밀도 98.30%로 제거했다고 보고했다. CARLA·Autoware 기반 시뮬레이션에서는 방어 미적용 시 발생한 허상 급정지와 후방 추돌이 적용 후에는 발생하지 않았다.

983b7c14e5337df9a2977564.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Differentially private zeroth-order optimization (DPZO) is a promising approach for privacy-preserving LLM fine-tuning, offering exceptional memory efficiency. Designing a practical DP procedure for selecting $C$ in DPZO is challenging because no fixed choice performs well across settings, straightforward search-based strategies suffer from poor utility and efficiency, and existing clipping-selection methods for DPSGD do not transfer well to DPZO due to its fundamentally different error regime. Our key idea is to avoid fine-tuning-based search by reducing clipping selection to a private quantile estimation problem, where the target quantile depends only on public privacy and training parameters. 47268c9c88c1af5201e8104b.title_original: ArguShield: Enforcing Minimum-Necessary Disclosure in Tool-Calling LLM Agents
47268c9c88c1af5201e8104b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents increasingly use third-party tools to complete user tasks. Even without malicious intent, they may fill broad or weakly constrained fields with private information that is unnecessary or inappropriate for the receiving tool. Such calls can satisfy the tool schema and complete the task, yet still violate minimum-necessary disclosure. We introduce ArguShield, a mediation layer that intercepts proposed tool calls before execution. It evaluates each candidate value using three signals: Value Provenance, Task Relevance, and Disclosure Boundary. ArguShield releases justified values, defers values that need user confirmation, and withholds those outside the permitted scope. We evaluate ArguShield with four tool-calling models on ArgPrivBench, a benchmark of 120 tasks across Travel, Shopping, and Healthcare. Unprotected agents frequently over-disclose private information despite high task success. Prompt-only protection reduces unauthorized disclosure but substantially lowers task success. ArguShield reduces unauthorized silent release to 9% on Standard tasks and 6% on High-risk tasks while preserving recoverable task success under simulated user confirmation.

7f8387b1d8339367c027eae5.title_original: Bounded Autonomy: A Trust-Anchored Defense Against Resource-Exhaustion Attacks on Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
7f8387b1d8339367c027eae5.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-augmented Large Language Model (LLM) agents are vulnerable to resource-exhaustion attacks that amplify model-token consumption through persistent context amplification, large tool output amplification, and error-induced agentic loops. Meanwhile, existing general-purpose agent defense frameworks, which address a broader range of security threats, often rely on prompt-level safeguards or coarse-grained resource limits and lack deterministic runtime mechanisms for controlling token consumption. They also provide limited support for balancing fault recovery against the risk of repeated resource-consuming execution. To address these limitations, we propose a trust-anchored closed-loop defense framework consisting of four phases: certificate-guided orchestration with deterministic handoffs, calibrated one-time node budgeting, Gateway-based runtime enforcement, and bounded recovery through a shared, non-resettable recovery pool. By accounting for both input and output tokens across all model invocations, our experiments demonstrate that the framework bounds cumulative token consumption, mitigates resource-amplification attacks, and preserves benign task utility under trusted execution assumptions.

e801bf0dceec64bf48f4415b.title_original: PLATRS: A Lattice-Based Linkable Accountable Ring Signature for Permissioned Blockchains
e801bf0dceec64bf48f4415b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Permissioned-ledger cross-domain data sharing needs anonymity and accountability: an endorsement hides its author, but a regulator must identify it on authorization reuse. b404fb162c69d926821c006f.title_original: From Dependent Ciphertexts to Sharp Bounds for Polynomial Evaluation in BGV
b404fb162c69d926821c006f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central challenge in Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is the selection of ciphertext moduli, which depends on accurately estimating noise growth during homomorphic evaluation. a8549b18e33f77d6dea7f0dc.title_original: POMA: Beyond Final Flags -- Process-Level Evaluation of Base LLMs in Vulnerability Exploitation
a8549b18e33f77d6dea7f0dc.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) evolve from text generation to autonomous software-engineering execution, automated vulnerability exploitability verification has emerged as a vital frontier in software quality assurance and security validation. 63cb8071058f4ad9bc58e23f.title_original: Bug Bounty Programs in the AI Era: How Does Platform Anti-Spam Friction Affect Vendor Profitability?
63cb8071058f4ad9bc58e23f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Since 2023, bug bounty platforms have introduced participation rules, such as proof-of-concept mandates, against a flood of AI-generated low-quality submissions. The platforms set these rules, but vendors running programs on them bear the cost when a vulnerability goes unreported and gets exploited. We ask whether the rules benefit the vendors they are meant to protect. Adding to Gal-Or, Hydari, and Telang's 2024 model a vendor triage cost per report reviewed and a participation cost paid in effort by the researchers reporting vulnerabilities, we locate a threshold in an effective triage-burden parameter, which captures the vendor's processing burden per unit of aggregate search effort, with the rules lowering profit below it and raising it above. Because attackers never use the platform, the participation cost falls on researchers alone and fewer take part. Bug-finding coverage falls and breach damage rises, which costs the vendor, while its triage bill falls, which helps.

b7aa9dc16c4157c0fe21c81c.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Software engineering (SE) agents can complete diverse engineering tasks by interacting with the development environment via tools that access files, run commands, and download resources. Existing defenses that analyze the agent trajectory may fail to detect such attacks, as they inspect only the initial prompt and the sequence of tool calls, but not the actual actions that are executed in the environment. This paper presents AgentBouncer, a novel runtime enforcement system that prevents SE agents from performing malicious actions by mediating, and if necessary denying, system calls that agents trigger via tool calls. The core of AgentBouncer is an LLM arbiter that judges system calls along two axes, necessity and safety for the current task. It denies unsafe system calls, and the less necessary a system call appears, the more certain the arbiter has to be about its safety to allow it. To manage runtime overhead, preseeded policy rules and hierarchy-aware caching ensure that the LLM arbiter is only invoked for key decisions. We evaluate AgentBouncer on a dataset of 340 attacks on the development environment, covering four attack vectors, combined with benign issue resolution tasks from SWE-bench Verified. c2372879820d8eb609d1e857.title_original: Complying with Cybersecurity Legislation: NIS2 Challenges and Industry Case Study
c2372879820d8eb609d1e857.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given the ever-increasing dependency on interconnected digital systems, cybersecurity has become a major concern. To protect markets and societies, governmental entities are developing legislation to enhance cyber resilience across sectors, introducing new technical and legal requirements. The NIS2 Directive, a revised version of the European-wide cybersecurity legislation, entered into force on 16 January 2023. Member States were required to adopt and publish transposing measures by 17 October 2024 and apply them from 18 October 2024. Specific obligations for essential and important entities are set out in national legislation. At the same time, other organizations, while not legally bound, seek to improve their cybersecurity maturity in alignment with EU-wide advances, for which NIS2 serves as a key reference. This paper presents the work conducted within a large European enterprise to align itself with the NIS2 Directive, focusing on how organizations can analyze and interpret its provisions to drive concrete technical and organizational improvements. A systematic methodology is applied to frame the company within the NIS2 context, identify relevant requirements, and derive actionable measures. Beyond outlining the technical steps taken, the work highlights the challenges of translating legislative requirements into practical implementations, emphasizing the use of existing IT resources while accounting for key legal aspects.

280ae4f561a184786d0f3245.title_original: Demystifying Detectors Guarding Agent Skill Hubs
280ae4f561a184786d0f3245.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent Skills has gained widespread adoption as an open standard for extending agent capabilities. To facilitate skill sharing, public skill hubs have grown in popularity and increasingly rely on automated security detectors to identify malicious skills at scale. Yet, the effectiveness and limitations of these detectors remain insufficiently understood. To fill this gap, we present the first systematic study of four hub-adopted and two community-provided malicious skill detectors on 1477 agent skills from seven datasets. Our evaluation reveals that even the best-performing hub-adopted detector by overall F1, skill-scanner with Qwen3.6, still misses 4.9% of malicious skills and incorrectly flags 17.8% of benign skills. To understand these failures, we manually analyze detectors' findings and decision-making processes, identifying two recurring failure mechanisms. False positives often arise when detectors flag sensitive operations, such as credential access, without considering whether they serve the skill's legitimate purpose. Conversely, false negatives occur when detectors recognize malicious instructions or behaviors but underestimate their severity or dismiss valid findings during review, ultimately leaving malicious skills unblocked. Guided by this analysis, we refine the prompts of a state-of-the-art detector, skill-vetter, improving its mean F1 score in eight of nine evaluation settings, with gains of up to 22.7 percentage

76c62788efc9eef438d488a1.title_original: Carried-Over and Agent-Native Threats in the Supply Chain of LLM Agent Skills
76c62788efc9eef438d488a1.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills are reusable packages that extend a large language model (LLM) agent with scripts, third-party dependencies, and natural-language instructions. 01c3627fa1db92d5a6bcfdbd.title_original: Airlock: Robust Sandboxing and Governance of Rogue Agents
01c3627fa1db92d5a6bcfdbd.excerpt: arXiv:2611.31010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent incidents involving agents bypassing sandboxing and network isolation have raised concerns about existing agent harnesses, prompting frontier labs such as OpenAI to reevaluate the security of their training platforms. Incident reviews show that determined agents can escape processes, containers, and VMs, or bypass their isolation through advanced side and covert channels. Follow-up audits also found that some agents concealed their actions by disabling monitoring and tampering with logs. We propose Airlock, an architecture that pairs each agent's VM with an Airlock VM, each running in a separate hardware-isolated Trusted Execution Environment (TEE). The Airlock VM fully mediates the agent's interactions with the outside world, including network and storage operations. We modify the firmware layer of Arm's Confidential Computing Architecture, Realm Management Monitor (RMM), and the kernels of both VMs so that the Airlock VM serves the agent VM's IO without involving the host. We adapt OpenShell, an agent runtime supporting sandboxing and governance policies, to this architecture. Airlock keeps network and filesystem policies, and credential protection effective even if the agent VM is fully compromised, and it removes the host from the agent's IO path, reducing opportunities for collusion and covert channels with the host. d42064810a86d614f003066b.title_original: CenShaper: Shaping Proxy Traffic for Censorship Circumvention
d42064810a86d614f003066b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.31016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern commodity DPI systems are capable of analyzing packet sizes, directions, and timings to detect circumvention tools even when those tools use sophisticated obfuscation. The anti-censorship community has called for innovation in traffic shaping and built an ecosystem that facilitates the adoption of new shaping techniques. However, a fundamental gap is halting progress: \textit{what} should circumvention traffic look like? Past experience with traffic shaping has underscored that effective shaping must produce traffic that looks like legitimate Internet traffic while limiting the ability of censors to identify multiple proxies through shared fingerprints. Combining these empirical observations with past experience with traffic shaping, we build CenShaper, which shapes each proxy's traffic to look like a selected TLS server. To reproduce these server-specific patterns, CenShaper trains a shared generative model using traffic from TLS connections to many servers and adapts it for each proxy using a small sample of recorded connections to its selected server. Our model evaluation shows that fingerprints learned from known proxies transfer poorly to proxies imit

fab75419afedef943134f1da.title_original: The Privacy Cost of Writing an Audit Receipt Before Its Context Is Known
fab75419afedef943134f1da.excerpt: arXiv:2611.31122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An audit recorder must permit exact recovery with a small private index before it knows which questions a future reader will ask. A recursion on question partitions generates the decision trees, their eventwise costs and the price equations. A common-optimal-tree criterion explains when reduction to a fractional cover preserves the result. On uniform binary linear event spaces with four private roles, if every quartet is split evenly by some bit, optimal identification probability at expected follow-up budget $b$ is $(1+b)/2$. Otherwise it is $\min(1/2+b/3,3/4)$. We characterize all priors attaining the latter curve in its rising regime and derive a closed-form compiler for three binary fields. For a population tilted by one pairwise parity we obtain the full budget curve and a single recorder attaining it. On eight negotiated TLS suites the aligned populations allow a 60 percent follow-up rate at a 70 percent identification ceiling. A pairwise correlation with unchanged marginal field frequencies reduces that maximum to 40 percent. Across 960 local TLS sessions, the recorder recovered every negotiated suite using two private bits per session.

87faa0344e0ca0c1c701cc42.title_original: Code-Based Message Authentication with Statistical Guarantees via Coordinate Selection and Masking
87faa0344e0ca0c1c701cc42.excerpt: arXiv:2611.31178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study message authentication over a public channel against a computationally unbounded adversary. Motivated by low-complexity applications, we consider schemes that leverage off-the-shelf binary linear codes already used for error correction in communication systems. Existing code-based constructions derive an authentication tag primarily from a single symbol in a $q$-ary code, which limits the tag length. However, selecting several binary coordinates allows a fixed binary linear code to support different tag lengths. We characterize how coordinate selection and ordering affect the statistical guarantees against impersonation and substitution attacks. In particular, we explore three methods: the subset selector, the ordered selector, and the independent selector. They read uniformly chosen coordinates in a fixed public or a secret random order, or with replacement, and add a uniform mask. With a fresh key per message, all three achieve the optimal impersonation probability $2^{-l_t}$ for $l_t$-bit tags. We bound the subset selector's substitution probability using only nonzero weights. Those of the other two depend only on the code length $n$, $l_t$, and the nonzero weight farthest from $n/2$. The independent selector achieves $2^{-l_t}$ for substitution when all nonzero weights equal $n/2$. Finally, we evaluate first-order Reed-Muller and Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem dual subcodes.

2ad68344abd4fb0393c9a3c1.title_original: SecretSifter: A Runtime Secret-Detection Engine for Live Web Traffic
2ad68344abd4fb0393c9a3c1.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28168v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Credentials embedded in client-delivered web artifacts, such as minified JavaScript bundles, webpack chunks, server-side-rendered state objects, and JSON or XML API responses, form a runtime attack surface that repository-time (shift-left) secret scanners do not observe, because the credential enters the served artifact at build time or at runtime, after every source-code gate has passed. This paper presents SecretSifter, an open-source runtime secret-detection engine that inspects live web traffic and reports secret-grade credentials at the point they are delivered to the browser. The engine combines format-anchored and context-gated detection rules, semantic key-name extraction, Shannon-entropy scoring, and dedicated detection of hardcoded CryptoJS/AES material across the full served surface. SecretSifter ships as three editions over one shared detection core: a Burp Suite extension, a Chrome extension, and a standalone Windows and macOS desktop application, with a Bearer-authenticated REST and MCP interface for automation. On a 198-value benchmark of real production client-exposed values (GT-198), the deterministic detection stage reached 79.8% recall at 86.8% precision in default configuration, the highest F1 of any system evaluated. The detection core is released under an open-source (MIT) license, and a de-identified reproducibility bundle and a public synthetic demo target are provided.

28a953e244319f871f0f2493.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28345v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Latent dynamic world models have proven to be highly versatile tools for embodied artificial intelligence systems, enabling online action planning, safe policy evaluation, and scalable policy learning. However, this versatility makes world models a vulnerable and centralized point of failure as a compromised model can impact planning, evaluation, and training at once. Therefore it is critical that the security and robustness properties of world models are properly understood before they are universally deployed in embodied AI systems. In this work we take a unifying approach towards this understanding, developing two novel attacks against world models, named state hallucination and dynamic shift attacks, aimed directly at impacting downstream systems, and proposing a new theoretical lens through which to study the robustness of latent dynamic world models. Through our analysis we identify robust latent space encoders as the key component of robust world models. We empirically validate this finding on four separate latent dynamic world model families, studying Dino World Model, Le World Model, r2Dreamer, and Cosmos 3, demonstrating significant improvements in robustness through adversarial encoder model training.

74bd87ae2d8794cb02455b60.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28460v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study stochastic convex optimization with heavy-tailed stochastic gradients under $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-user-level differential privacy, which protects each user's entire collection of samples. As a byproduct of our algorithmic developments, we obtain tight bounds for user-level private mean estimation under norm-moment assumptions, improving over the guarantees of Esfandiari et al. (2025), we close their remaining approximate-DP gap by removing the additional $d/\varepsilon$ user requirement and attaining the optimal sample complexity up to logarithmic factors.

046d66d6e4dfc3dabda132d4.title_original: APUF-SNG: A Low-Cost Arbiter-PUF Stochastic Number Generator with Tunable Output Probability
046d66d6e4dfc3dabda132d4.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28605v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stochastic computing (SC) encodes numerical values as probabilistic bit-streams and enables arithmetic operations using simple logic gates, offering a promising paradigm for low- cost, fault-tolerant, and highly parallel computation. By selecting input challenges that drive the path delay difference toward a target value, the resulting output probability is governed by intrinsic device noise, eliminating the need for conventional random-number generators and comparator-based SNGs. The proposed design inherits the low hardware overhead and statistical independence properties of the APUF structure. A probabilistic model and a challenge selection method are developed to characterize and control the stochastic behavior. b300f09428dcc72c60105441.title_original: HiPerfCC-KVCache: Accelerating Confidential LLM Serving with Hierarchical KV Caching
b300f09428dcc72c60105441.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28702v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hierarchical key-value (KV) caching reduces repeated prefill computation in large language model serving by retaining reusable state beyond GPU memory. Implemented in SGLang, HiPerfCC-KVCache uses existing protected transfer interfaces without hardware or driver changes. a788ab219904a0b852a0b091.title_original: Zero-Trust Formal Methods: AI Agents Build Verified Checkers for Untrusted Solvers
a788ab219904a0b852a0b091.excerpt: arXiv:2611.28704v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI coding agents now generate code faster than humans can review it. c1ee96f4283df74fa74b94a1.title_original: Q-TRACE: Physics-based zero-day attack detection for decoy-state quantum key distribution

b2345ec3a2309aa8b590cea3.title_original: Rateless Lattice Codes over Fading Wiretap Channels: Finite-Length Secrecy and the Secret-Key Capacity of Degraded Sessions
b2345ec3a2309aa8b590cea3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In rateless transmission the transmitter keeps sending until the legitimate receiver (Bob) can decode. If only their statistics are known, choosing the key length after the session guarantees a prescribed secrecy-outage probability. 4170be9563b61ad43b7e9e01.title_original: Ziv Meets Sumcheck: Zero-Knowledge Proofs of Floating-Point LLM Inference
4170be9563b61ad43b7e9e01.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29188v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Zero-knowledge proofs can show that a neural network produced a given output without revealing the network, but current systems for language models prove integer approximations of the model rather than the floating-point arithmetic that is actually deployed. Proving floating-point matrix multiplication has been regarded as hard, because rounding after every addition makes the result depend on the order of the additions. We avoid this obstacle by proving the correctly rounded product, in which every dot product is computed exactly and rounded once. This result is independent of the hardware and at least as accurate as standard kernels. We give an interactive proof for this relation whose cost is close to that of integer matrix multiplication, with roughly a thousand times fewer committed values than per-operation floating-point circuits need constraints, extend it to every layer of a transformer, and give a privacy construction for the complete argument whose zero knowledge we prove under explicit hypotheses. We implement the system and prove the full forward pass of GPT-2 small, including all twelve blocks and the output over the whole vocabulary, in 19 minutes on two processor cores; verification takes 21 seconds. The verifier rejects all 236 attacks we tested, and the model's outputs agree with high-precision inference at least as closely as standard 16-bit inference does.

069caf91e0a9dc5da1985e27.title_original: Near-Field Physical-Layer Authentication Under Noisy Enrollment
069caf91e0a9dc5da1985e27.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29292v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In near-field physical-layer authentication (PLA), the receiver estimates a spatial reference from noisy enrollment pilots. With a fixed residual-energy threshold, even a small reference error can cause the false rejection (FR) probability to approach one as the received energy increases. We derive the distribution of the overlap between the true and enrolled spatial directions and use it to calibrate a test based on the aligned energy and the residual-to-aligned energy ratio. The calibration bounds FR for arbitrary regional gains and all legitimate received energies above a prescribed minimum. For a fixed enrolled reference, we reduce the problem of finding the maximum acceptance probability of a multi-antenna attacker to a one-dimensional search. We also derive a pre-enrollment upper bound that holds when the attacker chooses its precoder after observing the enrolled reference. For a single region and a fixed angular threshold, the enrollment energy sufficient to preserve angular separation grows inversely with the square of the available angular margin. In the numerical study with 128 receive elements at 28 GHz, the FR upper bound was 0.9984, including the enrollment outage allowance. At a regional phase perturbation of 20, four regions provided the best trade-off among the tested partitions: its simulated FR was 0.1442, while its false acceptance (FA) at 9 m was 1.084 under the fixed transmit-energy setting.

ebe8acbc2de0184156e1b3f8.title_original: Feed-Forward Dimension Control for High-Dimensional Quantum Key Distribution over Time-Varying Airborne Free-Space Links
ebe8acbc2de0184156e1b3f8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29583v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High-dimensional quantum key distribution tolerates more noise than qubit-based protocols, but the dimension that maximizes the secret key depends on turbulence, background light, device imperfections, and block size, all of which change during an airborne or satellite pass. Here, a controller sets the dimension, acceptance thresholds, and key length of each block using only public data from earlier blocks. The controller estimates turbulence from observed error rates, maximizes the expected key under forecast uncertainty, and recalibrates its model online. We evaluate it on a simulated entanglement-based orbital-angular-momentum link between an aircraft and a ground station, using Kolmogorov phase screens and the Hufnagel--Valley turbulence profile. Accounting for forecast uncertainty increases the key by 31\%--47\% relative to a naive planner. Over night, dawn, daytime, and model-mismatch scenarios, the recalibrated controller retains at least 98.8\% of the key obtained with the best fixed dimension for each scenario,

aaa32c54177c7e4dcbc378b8.title_original: Contamination at the Operating Point: Train-Test Identity Overlap Inflates Low-FMR Face Recognition Accuracy by an Order of Magnitude
aaa32c54177c7e4dcbc378b8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29629v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Face verification systems are deployed by selecting a decision threshold that achieves a target false match rate (FMR); performance is then reported as the corresponding false non-match rate (FNMR). c863a8507d96f2d35539c15b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29925v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a new coding-theoretic problem motivated by censorship resistance. We call such codes $(\ell, s)$-unshardable. Intuitively, such codes prevent an adversary from selectively censoring individual pieces of data by erasing codeword symbols, without destroying large amounts of other data as collateral damage. We show that codes whose generator matrix has certain superregularity properties are unshardable. Using this connection, we construct linear codes that are $(\ell, s)$-unshardable with $s = (1-\varepsilon)k$ and locality $\ell = O_\varepsilon(1)$. 10a2aa90e282b4b4a66cff60.title_original: Tracing Attacker Diversity Reduction in Adaptive LLM Red Teaming
10a2aa90e282b4b4a66cff60.excerpt: arXiv:2611.29960v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning can increase the success of automated red teaming but it also narrows the attack vector. This study asks where in the attacker-defender-judge learning loop does the narrowing begin and which mechanisms lead to a narrowing attack. A frozen defender narrows attack diversity retention (ADR) earlier 0.496 relative to co-trained 0.891 at iteration twelve. Defender updates delay narrowing but dont prevent it. Successful attacks ("winners") have narrower attack diversity than the full set of generated attacks. Attacks closest to previous winners succeed 10-15 percentage points more often than those closest to previous failures. This winner-neighbor advantage holds after a defender update and for a fixed defender too. Attacks with a common opening have a common-opening advantage of 5-16 percentage points. The training row cap and update size account for little impact on ADR, and attack length accounts for only part of the ADR decrease. Narrowing appears to originate from the success only reward through the group-relative training advantage to the attacker update, with a persistent success edge setting the direction.

578bf76b9a68fdbeae6bff8e.title_original: Super-Multiplicativity of the Noncommutative Minimum and Applications to Quantum Privacy and Hypothesis Testing

b005764355f2747dee884351.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30146v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give polynomial-time algorithms for Gaussian multi-sampling under approximate $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differential privacy, with optimal sample complexity up to logarithmic factors. Our main construction uses $\widetilde{O}(m+d\sqrt{m}/\varepsilon)$ independent input samples from a $d$-dimensional Gaussian $P$ with unknown mean and covariance to generate $m$ exactly independent outputs. Their joint distribution is $\alpha$-close in total variation to $P^{\otimes m}$. Our lower bounds hold even for dependent outputs under the same joint accuracy guarantee, showing that exact independence incurs no additional sample cost beyond logarithmic factors. The single-sampler of Iverson, Kamath, and Mouzakis [COLT 2025] uses $\widetilde{O}(d/\varepsilon)$ input samples. Running it on a separate input dataset for each of $m$ outputs therefore costs $\widetilde{O}(md/\varepsilon)$ in total. Our construction reduces this dimension-dependent sample cost from linear to square-root dependence on the number of outputs. Our approach builds on the stable weighted statistics of Brown, Hopkins, and Smith [COLT 2023], also used for Gaussian single-sampling by Iverson, Kamath, and Mouzakis. To control privacy loss when the entire batch shares these statistics, we compare the joint output densities and obtain a privacy bound that scales with the square root of the batch size. The stability step downweights influential records and can reject the enti

cc953fab586ee2b1f5882c32.title_original: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage?
cc953fab586ee2b1f5882c32.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30483v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI agents now run statements against production databases, and several of the incidents that followed deleted production data, which came back only through backups or the provider's help. We ask what decides the damage when such an agent makes a mistake: the model, a guard layer in front of the database, or the database engine itself. The study has two preregistered layers. In Layer A, a frozen library of 22 canonical mistakes is applied by script, with no model involved, to four relational engines under five permission arms and two recovery arms, followed by an engine-native recovery drill (792 cells; 874 drill runs including 10-minute repeats). In Layer B, a minimal tool-calling agent driven by six small open-weight models (4B to 12B parameters, plus one 35B mixture-of-experts model with about 3B active, served locally) works on tasks that contain hazards across nine engines: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, ClickHouse, Apache Cassandra, MongoDB, Valkey, Apache Kafka and OpenSearch (9,468 trials). A secondary run added MariaDB, Redis and Elasticsearch (2,916 trials); each behaved like its closest core engine. Out of the box, the engines differ less in what a mistake destroys than in what they let you undo. Three of the seven preregistered hypotheses met their decision rule: H2 (for one of nine damage classes) and H3 largely by construction of the arms, and H4 only under its original measure. Four did not; one of them (H5) was unin

28a643a41fb0b76aef3676ea.title_original: Queuing for Secrets: Model-Based Remote Timing Attacks
28a643a41fb0b76aef3676ea.excerpt: arXiv:2611.30513v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Remote timing attacks exploit variations in response times to infer sensitive information about remote systems. Their effectiveness, however, is often limited by the difficulty of accurately modeling the stochastic nature of server-side response times, taking into account the intrinsic variability of the service time of a request and the impact of varying workloads on the observed response times. In this article, we propose a new stochastic framework for remote timing attacks based on queuing models and Bayesian statistics. We assume that the attacker knows the service time distributions of two classes of requests and that the information leakage occurs when a malicious observer can distinguish with high probability the class based on the observed response times in the presence of noise induced by exogenous workload. Our experimental evaluation on popular websites demonstrates the practical viability of the approach: our attack outperforms formal techniques based on deterministic service times and existing empirical techniques, while requiring less tuning and fewer hyper-parameters compared to previous formal approaches. Overall, our results show that principled stochastic modeling can provide a solid foundation for building more effective remote timing attacks under realistic network and workload conditions.

9efa85a218f4e6226dc0a772.excerpt: arXiv:2611.31208v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how to represent and randomize points in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space to obtain accurate bipartite matchings under metric privacy. Given $n$ private and $n$ public points, we analyze local mechanisms that randomize each private point or its distances to the public points. Using the public points' affine span, we construct a smaller representation that preserves all matching costs. When a trusted server receives the private points, we establish privacy and utility guarantees for Gumbel matching, which randomizes edge costs and releases only the assignment. Through upper bounds and worst-case constructions, we establish the tight rate $\Theta\!\left(n\min\{d,\log n\}/\varepsilon\right)$ for expected cost above the nonprivate optimum. Benchmark experiments support $d\approx\log n$ as a practical guide to the transition between directly randomizing point coordinates and using Gumbel matching. Extensions to squared Euclidean costs enable private nonparametric two-sample hypothesis testing. These results show how the application's trust model guides representation and dimension choices for better utility: under local privacy, low-dimensional point representations reduce excess cost, while under central privacy, distance representations achieve the optimal rate even in high dimension.

1d90872e349a1311e549f9c5.title_original: VideoMark: A Distortion-Free Robust Watermarking Framework for Video Diffusion Models
1d90872e349a1311e549f9c5.excerpt: arXiv:2504.16359v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work presents VideoMark, a training-free watermarking framework for video diffusion models with frame-aligned 2D VAEs. VideoMark embeds pseudorandom error-correcting (PRC) codewords by modulating the signs of Gaussian initialization noise without model retraining. Under a joint pseudorandomness assumption on the instantiated PRC encoder, the resulting initialization tensor is computationally indistinguishable from the Gaussian reference; exact distributional equality holds for the ideal independent uniform-sign construction. To support temporally structured video watermarking, we introduce a frame-wise message design together with a Temporal Matching Module (TMM), which recovers frame correspondence under temporal reordering without requiring length-specific watermark layouts. Experiments on ModelScope and I2VGen-XL show that VideoMark achieves accurate watermark extraction on clean generations while maintaining video quality comparable to watermark-free generation. The proposed temporal matching mechanism further improves recovery under frame reordering and enables systematic evaluation under a range of temporal and compression perturbations. We additionally analyze the computational characteristics and practical operating conditions of inversion-based extraction. Overall, VideoMark provides a simple training-free construction for studying pseudorandom watermarking in videos generated by frame-aligned 2D-VAE diffusion

b9259564d42db49525a401f1.title_original: LLM-Based Website Classification for Targeted Web Measurements
b9259564d42db49525a401f1.excerpt: arXiv:2510.08101v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Web measurements based on top lists of popular websites are a well-established methodology for assessing the security and privacy landscape of the Internet. However, existing top lists are unlabeled and lack semantic information about the nature of the included websites, forcing researchers to rely on custom techniques to focus on specific website classes of interest. This makes targeted web measurements, e.g., over shopping websites, challenging to carry out. In this paper, we investigate the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) to enable targeted web measurement studies. Building on prior literature, we identify key website classification tasks relevant to web measurements and highlight limitations in state-of-the-art classification approaches. We thus construct more carefully curated datasets to evaluate different LLMs on these tasks using standard performance measures. Our results show that LLMs can achieve strong performance across multiple classification scenarios, but the choice of the model and its configuration play a significant role in both the quality and the efficiency of the classification process. Finally, we use LLMs to emulate the setup of a targeted web measurement by automatically detecting adult websites in a subset of the Tranco list, without any need for custom techniques for dataset construction. Together, our benchmark evaluation and case study show that LLMs can enable high-quality targeted web measur

87b829920d718e80d13e54cf.title_original: zk-Agreements: A Privacy-Preserving Way to Establish Deterministic Trust in Confidential Agreements
87b829920d718e80d13e54cf.excerpt: arXiv:2510.20007v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Digital transactions currently exceed trillions of dollars annually, yet traditional paper-based agreements remain a bottleneck for automation, enforceability, and dispute resolution. Natural language contracts introduce ambiguity, require manual processing, and lack computational verifiability, all of which hinder efficient digital commerce. Computable legal contracts, expressed in machine-readable formats, offer a potential solution by enabling automated execution and verification. Blockchain-based smart contracts further strengthen enforceability and accelerate dispute resolution; however, current implementations risk exposing sensitive agreement terms on public ledgers, raising serious privacy and competitive intelligence concerns that limit enterprise adoption. We introduce zk-agreements, a protocol designed to transition from paper-based trust to cryptographic trust while preserving confidentiality. Our design combines zero-knowledge proofs to protect private agreement terms, secure two-party computation to enable private compliance evaluation, and smart contracts to guarantee automated enforcement. Together, these components achieve both privacy preservation and computational enforceability, resolving the fundamental tension between transparency and confidentiality in blockchain-based agreements.

1957af40c51e5b3983516407.title_original: FlowSteer: Prompt-Only Workflow Steering Exposes Planning-Time Vulnerabilities in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
1957af40c51e5b3983516407.excerpt: arXiv:2605.11514v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) powered by large language models (LLMs) increasingly adopt planner--executor architectures, where planners convert prompts into subtasks, roles, dependencies, and routing paths. This flexibility enables adaptive coordination, but exposes an attack surface in workflow formation: prompts can shape agent organization without modifying MAS infrastructure. We study this risk through social influence probing workflows to identify high-impact subtasks and malicious-signal propagation. The analysis reveals two vulnerabilities: workflow position can amplify or suppress a malicious signal, and sycophantic framing makes downstream agents more likely to relay it. We translate these findings into FlowSteer, a prompt-only workflow steering attack that converts vulnerability priors into one crafted prompt. FlowSteer aligns a malicious signal with influential task components and guides replanning toward dependencies that preserve propagation. Experiments show that FlowSteer increases malicious success by up to 55% over naive prompting, transfers across MAS setups, and remains effective with black-box topology inference. As FlowSteer biases the planning signals that generate the workflow, MAS defenses that inspect only the generated workflow provide limited protection. As such, we introduce FlowGuard, an input-side defense that reduces malicious success by up to 34% while preserving prompt utility. Our results posit

4e5954588690080f2a7baa23.title_original: WHET: Welding Homomorphic Encryption to Accelerator Architectures
4e5954588690080f2a7baa23.excerpt: arXiv:2606.11541v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables computations on encrypted data without decryption, offering strong data privacy at the expense of substantial computational and memory overheads. Prior efforts have steadily improved FHE performance through cryptographic and algorithmic enhancements or hardware acceleration, yet these two directions have progressed largely in isolation, hindering the full exploitation of available hardware capabilities. This work presents WHET, which introduces memory-centric, architecture-aware optimizations to better align cryptographic and algorithmic constructions with FHE accelerators. We first identify conventional FHE constructions as major sources of excessive working sets and heavy off-chip memory traffic. We propose accelerator-specific algorithmic techniques, including fine-grained coefficient-to-slot transformation, plaintext compression, and intermediate modulus raising, to reduce the on-chip data footprint by minimizing temporary ciphertexts and plaintext loads. With these techniques applied, we unveil additional opportunities to improve on-chip memory efficiency; we introduce lightweight architectural refinements, including a special-purpose buffer and functional unit extensions. With these optimizations, WHET achieves 1.38--8.74$\times$ per-area performance improvements over state-of-the-art FHE accelerators and the first-ever sub-millisecond CKKS bootstrapping.

243263781ef563995439e299.title_original: WoE Wrote It? Watermarking Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Black-Box Text Provenance
243263781ef563995439e299.excerpt: arXiv:2608.29151v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) watermarks provide a mechanism for text provenance, enabling model owners to identify machine-generated content and attribute it to a specific watermarked model. However, current LLM watermarking approaches predominantly rely on inference-time sampler methods and focus their analysis on dense models. Inference-time methods are only effective when the text is explicitly generated via the model owner's controlled API; they fail in a post-theft scenario. An adversary who steals or leaks the model weights gains complete control over inference and can simply run an unmodified sampler, bypassing the watermark and preventing post-theft attribution. In this work, we introduce Watermarking of Experts (WoE), a novel black-box text provenance method that leverages the unique structural properties of sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. WoE biases the vocabulary of a few secret experts, and defenders detect it by replaying suspect text through their own checkpoint to recover where these experts acted. This approach ensures the watermark remains intrinsic to the model parameters, enabling defenders to attribute text generated by stolen weights, leaked checkpoints, and secondary dense models distilled from the stolen model without needing access to the adversary's deployment or weights. We evaluate WoE across eight MoE models, demonstrating successful watermark detection from suspect text, achieving an averag

2dade55e09809a043107e4ee.title_original: Maverick: Private and Verifiable LLM Inference Made Practical via Matrix-Vector Multiplication Delegation
2dade55e09809a043107e4ee.excerpt: arXiv:2609.10264v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Open-source large language models (LLMs) are increasingly competitive with closed-source models while offering transparency and the ability to run inference without exposing user inputs to a service provider. However, running large-scale models locally requires substantial computational resources. In practice, users may still resort to a third-party provider, giving rise to privacy and correctness concerns. Existing solutions that address these problems often impose substantial server overhead or introduce additional trust assumptions. In this paper, we present Maverick, a novel approach to private and verifiable LLM inference based on a protocol for delegating matrix-vector multiplication, a dominant operation in LLMs. At its core, Maverick provides, to our knowledge, the first information-theoretically sound verification protocol for matrix-vector multiplication delegation with transparent preprocessing, efficient (batch) verification, and virtually no server overhead. We combine this verification primitive with LPN-based pseudorandom masking to provide input privacy. We implement Maverick and evaluate both of its modes on large open-source models. When only verification is required, Maverick lets commodity clients use models far beyond their own capacity: a laptop and a desktop with a 16 GB GPU generate tokens 81-270$\times$ faster on Qwen3-32B than with local inference, and reach 7-33 tokens per second on Llama 4, a 400B

224fe636566562c59cb46b04.title_original: On the Complexity of Symmetric Boolean Functions in Multiparty Private Simultaneous Messages
224fe636566562c59cb46b04.excerpt: arXiv:2610.21216v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multiparty Private Simultaneous Messages (PSM), also known as Decomposable Randomized Encoding (DRE) or information-theoretic garbling, is a model for non-interactive secure computation. Each party encodes its input using shared randomness and sends a message to an evaluator who must recover the function output without learning anything else about the inputs. Perfect privacy requires identical transcript distributions on inputs with the same output. We also study the weaker notion of support privacy, which requires only that these distributions have the same support. We study the communication complexity of symmetric Boolean functions when each of the n parties holds one input bit. Lower bounds. We prove a $(1-o(1))n\log n$ lower bound for support-private PSM protocols computing $OR_n$, which is known to be tight. As a consequence, we obtain the same lower bounds for $MAJ_n$ and $EMAJ_n$. We also prove an $\Omega(n\log q)$ lower bound for $MOD_q$. An alternative proof technique recovers most of these bounds as well as the previously known approach based on Nechiporuk's method. Upper bounds. We construct perfectly private and support private PSM protocols of total communication $\widetilde{O}(n^{3/2})$ and $\widetilde{O}(n)$ respectively for every symmetric Boolean function, improving on the known quadratic bound. For $MAJ_n$, known branching-program constructions yield an upper bound of $O(n\log^3 n\log\log n)$. For $EMAJ_n$

dbedd273594bbf930b8556b7.title_original: SPARSEBLEED: Bypassing Attribute-Inference Defenses via Sparsity Optimizations
dbedd273594bbf930b8556b7.excerpt: arXiv:2610.38110v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When a model trained on sensitive records is exposed through a prediction API, an attribute-inference attack (AIA) plugs each possible value of a missing field into a partially known record to infer which value belonged to the training record. Current defenses mask confidence scores and hide internal activations. We show that sparsity optimizations, software and hardware routines (sparse kernels) that skip arithmetic and memory fetches on zero activations or weights, reopen attribute inference through the execution footprint. We introduce SparseBleed, the first hardware and execution-based AIA on training data. Training makes neuron firing selective to sensitive attributes, so each candidate value activates a different set of neurons and sparse kernels skip the rest; the candidate value therefore sets how many multiply-accumulate operations execute and which weight columns are read, shifting response time and shared-hardware contention even when only a class label is returned. SparseBleed calibrates each candidate's footprint against reference measurements for that value. Across 11 CPU and GPU sparse libraries (e.g., Intel oneDNN-AMX, NVIDIA cuSPARSE), MLPs, and FT-Transformers up to 1.5B parameters, execution time on TACO varies by up to ~25,000 timer ticks across prediction-confidence levels. The strongest SparseBleed variant gains +16.4 points in mean accuracy over label-only LOMIA and +8.9 over confidence-based CSMIA, up

73af23d8318cff2c37c7636b.title_original: Fault Injection Attacks on Q-Learning: Analysis, Vulnerabilities, and Countermeasures
73af23d8318cff2c37c7636b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.16151v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hardware fault injection attacks threaten machine learning systems, yet their impact on reinforcement learning (RL) has received little attention despite the use of RL in safety-critical applications. This paper presents a security analysis of Q-Learning implementations under voltage and clock glitching attacks on a ChipWhisperer platform, evaluating five variants: Standard, Robust, Resilient, Linear, and Deep Q-Learning. In standard Q-Table implementations, faults corrupt reward computation, action selection, and Q-value updates during learning, and change the selected action during inference. Robust Q-Learning does not prevent these attacks: NaN and infinite values injected during learning persist in the Q-table, and its greedy policy uses the same code as standard Q-Learning. This paper also evaluates a Resilient Q-Learning variant that applies triple modular redundancy with majority voting. It corrects corruption of a single Q-table copy, but inputs shared by the copies, such as the reward, and the voting code itself remain outside its protection. The analysis extends to Linear and Deep Q-Learning, where faults corrupt stored weights during learning and change actions during inference. Moving beyond benchmark environments, this work evaluates an online traffic light controller in a microscopic traffic simulator, where a single injected infinite value degrades accumulated vehicle waiting time by 148x while corrupting unde

caad0bf6809497f60329e3c7.title_original: Anonymous in Name Only: A Critical Review and a Reidentification Exercise on the European Commission's Anonymization Measures for Google Search Data under Article 6(11) of the DMA
caad0bf6809497f60329e3c7.excerpt: arXiv:2611.17012v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In July 2026, the European Commission (EC) set out the anonymization measures Alphabet must implement to share Google Search data with competing search engines under Article 6(11) of the Digital Markets Act. As the first concrete illustration of how the EC operationalizes anonymization under the EU digital rulebook, this methodology could become a regulatory benchmark. In this paper, we show why it should not. We critically review the anonymization measures proposed by the EC, from the characterization of residual risk to the suppression thresholds and the reliance on contractual safeguards. For each of those issues, we highlight significant conceptual flaws, and, where applicable, we illustrate these flaws with empirical observations from real Google Search data provided by Alphabet and protected under the EC's measures. Importantly, we present examples of low-effort reidentification, record linkage, and confidential attribute inference achieved through straightforward and automatable attack patterns. Our findings show that the approach of the EC relies on unjustified heuristics rather than formal privacy guarantees, underestimates the risks inherent in free-text search queries, and sacrifices data utility without achieving meaningful protection. We also demonstrate that the proposed measures do not meet any of the three anonymization criteria established by the European Data Protection Board (EDPB): no record isolation, no

1a1a5016001cf76544305dac.title_original: Correctable Enrollment and One-Transaction Seed Proofs for Ethereum's Post-Quantum Migration
1a1a5016001cf76544305dac.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25663v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A quantum computer running Shor's algorithm can extract the private key of every Ethereum account whose public key is published, and accounts exposed by their own transactions hold 54.6% of execution-layer ETH. As the first such machine may stay secret, a migration cannot wait for visible thefts, and once keys are extractable, legacy signatures no longer tell owners from attackers. We design a migration in which owners enroll post-quantum keys cheaply with their existing signatures before ECDSA is retired at a scheduled time, while a zero-knowledge proof of the wallet's BIP-39 seed can correct any such enrollment until a common deadline afterward; an account nobody enrolled stays frozen and recoverable by seed proof without a deadline. Each proof binds the new key, a nonce and a fee cap, so neither a paying sponsor nor a reordering block builder can redirect or replay it. Validators switch to hash-based keys first, at a finalized checkpoint and under a stated bound on the attacker's voting power. We prove the account guarantees under explicit assumptions, model-check the rules, and implement the design in go-ethereum and a Lean consensus client. A three-layer recursive hash-based STARK yields a seed proof of about 190 KB that fits one transaction, verifies in 38 ms and takes a median of 111 s to generate on a laptop; four proofs aggregate into one. In a ten-node simulation with mainnet-derived accounts and fee demand, block

1d9eaef38d6510850055739d.title_original: ALIoTh: Orchestrating Multi-Agent LLMs for Autonomous IoT Penetration Testing
1d9eaef38d6510850055739d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25809v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Penetration testing in Internet of Things (IoT) environments, especially those composed of various different devices, e.g., smart plugs, smart cameras, and smart doors, presents great challenges across the phases of information gathering, attack surface enumeration, privilege escalation, and lateral movement. This paper introduces ALIoTh, a multi-agent, workflow-driven penetration testing framework that integrates Large Language Models agents within a Self-Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Self-RAG) architecture to autonomously identify and exploit vulnerabilities in IoT and Industrial-IoT (IIoT) environments. By leveraging state-of-the-art language models and orchestrating specialized agents via the LangGraph framework, ALIoTh dynamically plans and executes a full-spectrum offensive pipeline. This includes network, devices, and service enumeration, vulnerability assessment, payload generation, reverse shell deployment, and privilege escalation on each device. The Self-RAG mechanism equips expert agents with contextual access to IoT security knowledge, e.g., related documentation, tool manuals, and known attack techniques, enhancing their reasoning capabilities in scenarios involving multiple device exploitation and group policy manipulation.

369afe11281802fbb28db89f.title_original: RAVEN: A Self-RAG Based Agent for Threat Classification and Response
369afe11281802fbb28db89f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.25832v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Security event analysis in large enterprises can be overwhelming, as each alert typically requires manual in- spection by human operators. This process is time-consuming and prone to inconsistencies, especially in high-volume Secu- rity Operations Center (SOC) environments. In this work- in-progress paper, we present RAVEN: Retrieval-Augmented Vulnerability & Event aNalysis, an agentic framework designed to support SOC analysts by automating the initial stages of alert investigation. The proposed system leverages a Self- Reflective Retrieval-Augmented Generation-based approach to provide an initial classification of security events and enables interactive refinement through analyst-in-the-loop queries. Un- like traditional approaches that rely on generic mitigation strategies, RAVEN generates context-aware remediation sug- gestions by incorporating knowledge of the target enterprise infrastructure. We implement an early-stage prototype and report preliminary results on three balanced test sets of 400 curated web payloads each (SQLi, XSS, SSTI) and a qualitative case study of mitigation generation; an evaluation on IDS- generated alerts and a user study are ongoing and outlined as remaining work.

b950bb549aa5e900bb5a8854.title_original: Lightweight Detection and Model Attribution of Synthetic Speech via Residual Statistical Fingerprints
b950bb549aa5e900bb5a8854.excerpt: arXiv:2411.14013v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: As speech generation technologies advance, so do risks of impersonation, misinformation, and spoofing. We present a lightweight, training-free method for synthetic speech detection and source model attribution. Our method builds on model-specific fingerprints that are computed as the average of the differences between audio signals and their filtered versions, referred to as residuals. Leveraging the Mahalanobis distance of the residual for a given audio signal to these model-specific fingerprints allows to identify the source model as well as to distinguish real from fake audio. A broad set of experiments across multiple synthesis systems and languages demonstrate a supreme performance of the proposed approach on four tasks: open-world single-model attribution, closed-world multi-model attribution, real vs. synthetic speech classification, and out-of-domain detection.

0b58c0827cf37d8e88e95e65.excerpt: arXiv:2505.14914v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce the Sei Giga, a multi-concurrent producer parallelized execution EVM layer one blockchain. In an internal testnet Giga has achieved >5 gigagas/sec throughput and sub 250ms finality. Giga uses Autobahn for consensus with separate DA and consensus layers requiring f+1 votes for a PoA on the DA layer before consensus. Giga reaches consensus over ordering and uses async block execution and state agreement to remove execution from the consensus bottleneck.

b928c492131e36c030cded0c.title_original: MARGIN: Margin-Aware Regularized Geometry for Imbalanced Vulnerability Detection
b928c492131e36c030cded0c.excerpt: arXiv:2605.10240v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Software vulnerability detection is critical for ensuring software security and reliability. Despite recent advances in deep learning, real-world vulnerability datasets suffer from two severe challenges: frequency imbalance and difficulty imbalance. We reinterpret these challenges from an embedding geometry perspective, observing that such imbalances induce geometric distortions in hyperspherical representation space. To address this issue, we propose MARGIN, a metric-based framework that learns discriminative vulnerability representations through adaptive margin metric learning and hyperspherical prototype modeling. MARGIN dynamically adjusts geometric regularization according to the distribution structure estimated by the von Mises-Fisher concentration, aligning the probability mass of embedding distributions with their corresponding Voronoi cells, thereby reducing geometric distortion and yielding more stable decision boundaries. Extensive experiments on public vulnerability datasets show that MARGIN consistently outperforms strong baselines, achieving notable improvements in classification and detection, especially on challenging, imbalanced datasets. Further analysis demonstrates that MARGIN produces more structured embedding geometries, improving robustness, interpretability, and generalization.

ed3c43704502ef28f408ee99.title_original: Control and Cryptosystem Co-Design for Encrypted Nonlinear Multi-Agent Coordination
ed3c43704502ef28f408ee99.excerpt: arXiv:2606.07375v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A cloud that must not see the agents' states can steer them on data encrypted under CKKS, the approximate scheme for real-valued arithmetic. Its stored estimate admits only so many multiplications before a refresh that costs time and error, and every decrypted command is flooded with noise of a mandated size, constraints no controller designed in exact arithmetic meets. For networked agents with polynomial dynamics, we prove one closed-loop bound tying the controller and the cryptosystem in both directions. If the exact loop contracts on a region, the encrypted loop stays within a certified radius of it, set by the per-cycle and refresh errors, the refresh interval, the flooding and the delay. The errors and the bound's probability are derived from the library's circuits, not measured. Inverted, the bound turns the tolerance and a failure-probability target into the refresh interval, and with it the precision, security parameters and period. Conversely, costs shape the realization: a tracing backend tallies any pipeline's operations before a ciphertext exists, and evaluating the prediction about each agent's reference holds the released error below its sixteen-agent level. A full satellite-train mission encrypted at 128-bit security ran inside its certified radius, and the certificate holds across six graphs and at 32, 64 and 128 agents. Security enters the design twice, in time and precision. The cryptosystem is there

d0c40cfb8c4882fa55fbebd1.title_original: Benchmarking Quantum Machine Learning for Power-System Attack Detection: Evaluation Choices Can Decide the Outcome
d0c40cfb8c4882fa55fbebd1.excerpt: arXiv:2608.15617v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum machine learning is proposed to detect grid cyberattacks, but no study we could read tests quantum and classical detectors under white-box, transfer, and black-box attacks and random label flips in one protocol. We compare two quantum and six classical detectors on public grid-attack data under equal tuning budgets. Our main finding: evaluation choices can decide the outcome. On these data, seven choices each changed a reported result with model families fixed. Row-level splits inflate our best score by 0.31 macro-averaged F1 over held-out files, where matched-dimensionality classical and quantum models barely clear chance. Under its own white-box attack the quantum kernel's score falls from 0.56 to 0.01 (chance 0.50), while a transferred attack in the same run leaves 0.52. Trees admit no gradient-based white-box attack, so their attacked scores are upper bounds. These attack results use eight-dimension detectors under row-level splits. On gas-pipeline and simulated-grid data, neither quantum detector is more accurate or consistently more robust; three of the seven choices reproduce fully on gas data with one pressure feature log-scaled (two within noise), and none of the four checked on the grids does. Benchmarks should hold out whole files and give every model its own attack where possible. We release code and checklist.

7767a0bb6b0bc6a22cf406de.title_original: Spectrum-Aware Bounds on Invertibility for Privacy-Enhancing Instance Encoding
7767a0bb6b0bc6a22cf406de.excerpt: arXiv:2608.23382v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Instance encoding is a popular empirical technique for privacy enhancement when sharing data to an untrusted server. It transforms sensitive data through an encoding process before sharing, with the hope that the encoding process retains utility but makes it hard to reconstruct the original data. However, most work offers no theoretical guarantee that the encoding process is actually irreversible. A recent work derived a mean-squared error (MSE) bound limiting any adversary's reconstruction accuracy, offering one of the first theoretical results in this domain. This bound, however, has three critical limitations: it is often too loose, only works with randomized encoders (excluding many deterministic encoders practitioners use), and only bounds MSE. We introduce a family of new bounds that (1) are tighter, (2) applicable even to fully deterministic encoders, and (3) can extend beyond MSE to other norm-based similarity metrics, by properly accounting for the encoder's spectral structure. We evaluate our bounds across a range of encoders, datasets, and attacks, showing they hold consistently and improve upon the existing bound.

def05c6921270af4a276cfd7.title_original: High-Throughput Private Information Retrieval with on-CPU Accelerators
def05c6921270af4a276cfd7.excerpt: arXiv:2611.02376v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present AltoPIR, the first PIR system that exploits the capability of emerging on-CPU matrix accelerators such as Intel AMX. Unlike existing solutions, AltoPIR achieves high-performance PIR through efficient batching without requiring discrete accelerators. However, the on-CPU accelerator has only a few small registers and shares its core with request handling. As a result, it runs far below its peak rate while its operands arrive from memory, and it remains idle while its core handles requests. To keep the accelerator busy, we design mechanisms that reduce both the memory traffic of a batch and the core cycles spent on each request. It is the piecewise-linear interpolation of an explicit sequence of points generated by cost-optimally shifted truncated geometric masks, with infinitely many affine pieces accumulating at the critical budget, where the frontier meets the prior vulnerability with zero slope. When such an array is accessed with symbolic indices, DSA loses points-to field sensitivity for the entire object, inflating false alarms in the data-flow analysis. 8d72997fe127463e17495ff5.title_ko: Isaac Lab·Newton으로 Microduck 장애물 회피 학습하는 Sim2Real 절차 소개

8d72997fe127463e17495ff5.background_ko: 기존 보행 정책은 로봇의 균형을 유지하지만 경로상의 장애물을 피하도록 조향하지는 못해, 이를 보완하는 별도 회피 제어기를 학습한다.

1bcbeacecb48126acdc8ca89.summary_ko: Check Point는 이란 연계로 평가한 Volant Manticore가 키프로스의 통신사·항공사·핵심 기반시설과 사우디 의료기관을 노렸다고 밝혔다. 공격에는 IPFS 기반 명령·제어 백도어 KuboShell과 후속 침해 도구 Homa, 정상 원격관리 도구가 사용됐다. 연구진은 MuddyWater 출신 인력이 분리된 독립 조직일 가능성을 제시했다.
1bcbeacecb48126acdc8ca89.background_ko: 일부 공격에서는 AI로 만든 인물을 내세운 가짜 이력서로 전체 문서 다운로드 링크 클릭을 유도해 피해 시스템에 KuboShell을 설치했다.

176bb01293e6db21f16ce1b3.title_ko: ANY.RUN, 2027년 SOC 예산에서 AI 효과 측정·조사 효율화 강조
176bb01293e6db21f16ce1b3.summary_ko: ANY.RUN은 2027년 보안운영센터(SOC) 예산을 계획할 때 AI 기능 수보다 조사 시간과 업무량, 상위 분석 단계 이관 감소를 평가해야 한다고 제안했다. 자동화와 위협 인텔리전스 연계로 인력 증원에 앞서 기존 분석 역량을 확보하자는 내용이다. 경보 1,000건당 450시간을 절약할 수 있다는 수치는 업체 추정이며, 현금 비용 절감을 보장하지 않는다.
176bb01293e6db21f16ce1b3.background_ko: 경보와 조사 업무, 수작업 비용이 늘어나는 가운데 예산 제약과 투자 효과 입증 압박에 대응하기 위한 제안이다.

67f8dfd5d82984c883081f44.title_ko: Turnitin, 고객용 시스템 무단 접근 공개…정보 유출 여부 조사
67f8dfd5d82984c883081f44.summary_ko: Turnitin은 일부 고객용 시스템에서 무단 활동을 발견해 사고 대응 절차를 가동하고 외부 보안 전문가와 조사 중이라고 밝혔다. 회사는 시스템이 정상 운영되며 안전하다고 설명했지만, 사용자 데이터 접근·탈취 여부와 피해 규모, 발생 시점은 공개하지 않았다.

8133c225d226b5224cbfad19.title_original: Radware discloses breach exposing customer cloud access keys
8133c225d226b5224cbfad19.excerpt: Cybersecurity company Radware says attackers gained access to some of its customers' account details and cloud access keys through an unsecured internal Cloud WAF (Web Application Firewall) management API that was left exposed online. [...]
8133c225d226b5224cbfad19.title_ko: Radware, 인증 없는 내부 API 통해 고객 클라우드 접근 키 노출 가능성
8133c225d226b5224cbfad19.summary_ko: BleepingComputer가 입수한 Radware 보고서에 따르면, 인증 없이 공개된 내부 Cloud WAF 관리 API를 통해 고객 연락처와 일부 고객의 로그 내보내기용 자격 증명이 노출됐을 가능성이 있다. 회사는 API 접근을 차단하고 영향받은 고객에게 키 교체와 저장소 접근 기록 점검을 권고했다. 고객 애플리케이션 트래픽에 접근한 증거는 발견되지 않았다고 밝혔다.
8133c225d226b5224cbfad19.background_ko: 내부 전용 Cloud WAF 관리 API가 인증 없이 공용 인터넷에서 접근 가능한 상태로 노출돼 공격자의 무단 접근을 허용했다.

curation.reason_ko: Radware 고객의 클라우드 키 노출 가능성이 제기돼 키 교체와 접근 기록 점검이 요구된다.

c033aba3e996da788e81efee.title_original: ShinyHunters claims to return after FBI arrests, uses old PGP keys as proof
c033aba3e996da788e81efee.excerpt: The ShinyHunters extortion gang claims to have returned in posts on a new data leak site after a series of arrests over the past two months targeting alleged members. [...]
c033aba3e996da788e81efee.title_ko: ShinyHunters 복귀 주장…과거 PGP 서명 확인됐지만 운영진 동일성은 불명
c033aba3e996da788e81efee.summary_ko: ShinyHunters를 자처하는 운영진이 새 Tor 유출 사이트에서 복귀를 선언하고 과거 PGP 키로 서명한 검증 메시지를 게시했다. BleepingComputer는 서명의 유효성을 확인했지만, 이는 과거 개인키에 접근할 수 있다는 뜻일 뿐 기존 운영진과 동일 인물임을 입증하지는 않는다고 설명했다. 해당 키들은 이미 폐기됐고 여러 사람이 보유했다는 소문도 있다.
c033aba3e996da788e81efee.background_ko: 관련자로 지목된 인물들의 잇단 체포 이후 기존 대표와 연락이 끊기고 유출 사이트가 중단된 가운데 새 운영진이 복귀를 주장했다.

0e976d5b5eeb5e3973749719.title_original: European Commission confirms data theft in EU Academy breach
0e976d5b5eeb5e3973749719.excerpt: The European Commission, the European Union's main executive body, has confirmed that attackers breached its EU Academy online learning hub and stole the personal data of an undisclosed number of users. [...]
0e976d5b5eeb5e3973749719.title_ko: EU 집행위, EU Academy 침해로 이용자 이름·이메일 유출 확인
0e976d5b5eeb5e3973749719.summary_ko: 유럽연합 집행위원회가 온라인 학습 플랫폼 EU Academy 침해로 이용자의 이름과 이메일 주소가 유출됐다고 확인했다. 피해 규모는 공개되지 않았으며, 집행위는 플랫폼 공개 접근을 중단하고 이용자에게 피싱성 이메일과 메시지를 주의하라고 안내했다.

curation.reason_ko: 유럽연합 집행위원회가 EU Academy 침해와 이용자 개인정보 탈취를 확인했으나 피해 인원은 미공개다.

4252f119d456030bd840237e.title_original: Hackers compromise Check Point Servers in 22 organizations
4252f119d456030bd840237e.excerpt: Threat actors have exploited multiple vulnerabilities to compromise two dozen Check Point Security management servers in an ongoing campaign targeting 22 organizations. [...]
4252f119d456030bd840237e.title_ko: GreyNoise, 17개국 22개 조직의 Check Point 관리 서버 침해 포착

curation.reason_ko: GreyNoise가 17개국 조직의 관리 서버 침해와 자격증명 탈취·보안 정책 해제를 보고했다.

7d65750683943836da03353b.title_original: From Vulnerability Noise to Resilience: Rethinking Security in the AI Era
7d65750683943836da03353b.excerpt: AI-driven development is adding complexity to software supply chains, leaving security teams overwhelmed by vulnerabilities that may pose little actual risk. RapidFort explains how runtime visibility, container hardening, and automated remediation can reduce vulnerability noise and improve software resilience. [...]
7d65750683943836da03353b.title_ko: RapidFort 전략책임자 “취약점 개수보다 실제 실행·악용 가능성에 집중해야”
7d65750683943836da03353b.summary_ko: RapidFort의 George Manuelian은 취약점 개수나 CVSS 점수보다 실제 실행 여부와 도달·악용 가능성을 중심으로 보안 우선순위를 정해야 한다고 주장했다. 런타임 분석으로 불필요한 구성요소를 제거하고, 검증된 기반 이미지와 자동 재빌드를 CI/CD에 통합해 소프트웨어 공급망의 공격 표면을 줄이는 접근을 제안했다.
7d65750683943836da03353b.background_ko: AI 지원 개발이 코드 생성과 외부 패키지 도입을 가속하면서, 배포 소프트웨어의 의존성과 실제 사용 구성요소를 파악하기 어려워졌다는 문제의식이 배경이다.

2272bd3015e16a4b7f859526.title_original: McDonald's Japan data breach exposes customer location information
2272bd3015e16a4b7f859526.excerpt: McDonald's Japan, the fast-food giant's Japanese subsidiary, has disclosed a data breach after attackers accessed a database containing sensitive information for users of the company's official smartphone app. [...]
2272bd3015e16a4b7f859526.title_ko: 맥도날드 일본 앱 데이터 유출…고객 위치·구매 내역 노출
2272bd3015e16a4b7f859526.summary_ko: 맥도날드 일본 법인은 공식 스마트폰 앱 데이터베이스에 대한 무단 접근으로 구매 내역, IP 주소, 모바일 기기 위치 정보, 고객 관리 ID가 노출됐다고 밝혔다. 이름·연락처·신용카드 정보는 포함되지 않았으며, 피해 인원과 공격 탐지 시점은 공개하지 않았다. 회사는 무단 접근에 쓰인 인증 정보 무효화와 관련 시스템 조사를 진행 중이라고 설명했다.

6f25c07775b28ac9556046d2.title_original: New Shirudo tool uses AI to shield unpatched Linux systems from exploits
6f25c07775b28ac9556046d2.excerpt: OpenAI and Cisco launched an open-source Linux security tool named Shirudo that deploys temporary runtime protections to block vulnerability exploitation while administrators prepare and roll out patches, without restarting services. [...]
6f25c07775b28ac9556046d2.title_ko: OpenAI·Cisco, 패치 전 Linux 취약점 악용 막는 Shirudo 공개
6f25c07775b28ac9556046d2.summary_ko: OpenAI와 Cisco가 오픈소스 Linux 보안 도구 Shirudo를 공개했다. eBPF 기반 임시 보호 규칙을 서비스 재시작 없이 적용하며, AI가 규칙 개발·검증을 지원하되 배포는 사람이 통제한다. 연구진은 실행 중인 Elasticsearch를 중단하지 않고 공격을 차단했다고 밝혔지만, 커널에 영향을 줄 수 있는 규칙을 AI가 작성하는 데 대한 우려도 나왔다.
6f25c07775b28ac9556046d2.background_ko: 관리자가 패치를 준비하고 배포하는 동안에도 서비스를 재시작하지 않고 취약점 악용을 차단하도록 개발됐다.

03f361765c8648ac94ce505b.title_original: VMware Updates Patch Critical ESX, vCenter Vulnerabilities
03f361765c8648ac94ce505b.excerpt: The critical bugs include an authentication bypass in vCenter and flaws that could allow code execution on ESX hosts. The post VMware Updates Patch Critical ESX, vCenter Vulnerabilities appeared first on SecurityWeek .
03f361765c8648ac94ce505b.title_ko: Broadcom, VMware 취약점 23건 패치…ESX·vCenter 치명적 결함 포함
03f361765c8648ac94ce505b.summary_ko: Broadcom이 VMware 제품군의 취약점 23건을 수정하는 패치를 발표했다. vCenter의 인증 우회와 ESX의 호스트 코드 실행 관련 치명적 결함을 비롯해 Avi Load Balancer와 VMware Tools 문제도 포함됐다. vCenter 8.0 U3m에는 관련 수정이 이미 반영됐으며, 실제 공격 악용 여부는 공지에 언급되지 않았다.
03f361765c8648ac94ce505b.background_ko: ESX의 I/O 필터 서비스와 XHCI USB 컨트롤러에서 메모리 처리 결함이, vCenter의 VMware Directory Service에서 인증 우회 결함이 발견됐다.

curation.reason_ko: VMware 인증 우회와 호스트 코드 실행 관련 치명적 결함이 수정돼 운영 조직의 확인이 필요하다.

38d9d219c70082d770e07ce5.title_original: Anthropic Expands Enterprise Safeguards for Detecting AI Misuse
38d9d219c70082d770e07ce5.excerpt: EFS helps zero-retention customers spot Claude misuse spread across many requests while keeping conversation data in their own cloud. The post Anthropic Expands Enterprise Safeguards for Detecting AI Misuse appeared first on SecurityWeek .
38d9d219c70082d770e07ce5.title_ko: Anthropic, 여러 요청의 패턴으로 AI 악용 탐지하는 EFS 공개 베타
38d9d219c70082d770e07ce5.summary_ko: Anthropic이 AI 악용 탐지 체계 Enterprise Frontier Safeguards(EFS)의 공개 베타를 발표했다. 개별로는 정상처럼 보이는 여러 요청에서 의심스러운 패턴을 찾아 악의적 사용과 운영자 의도를 벗어난 에이전트 행동을 탐지하도록 설계됐다. 대화 데이터는 고객 클라우드에 보관하고 Anthropic은 내용 대신 모니터링 메타데이터를 받는다.

b2117a2c7b6e4d28bc7a4ae0.summary_ko: OpenAI와 Cisco가 AI 에이전트를 활용하는 오픈소스 보안 플랫폼 Shirudo를 공개했다. 두 회사는 에이전트가 eBPF 기반 보호 규칙을 생성·시험해 시스템 재시작 없이 취약점 악용을 차단하도록 설계했다고 설명했다. 특정 Linux 커널 기능과 추가 패치, TPM 2.0이 필요한 사전 출시 단계로, 아직 운영 환경에는 적합하지 않다.
b2117a2c7b6e4d28bc7a4ae0.background_ko: AI로 취약점 발견과 악용이 빨라지면서 패치 적용 압박이 커지자, 영구 패치를 설치하기 전 임시 보호를 제공하기 위해 개발됐다.

curation.reason_ko: AI가 Linux 보호 규칙을 만드는 Shirudo가 공개됐으며 운영 환경에 부적합한 사전 출시 단계다.

327951be6aabba295a801e5a.title_original: Machine-Generated Fake Plugin Turns WordPress Sites Into JavaScript Delivery Points
327951be6aabba295a801e5a.excerpt: The Wordfence Threat Intelligence Team recently analyzed a malware campaign that installs a fake WordPress plugin built almost entirely by a name generator. Various identifiers in the project – the plugin title, its directories and files, its PHP functions, variables and REST namespaces – are a machine-made compound of a prefix, a technology word and a suffix: trijavascriptly , ultravueal , maxdataic-quaddatasion . Behind the generated names is a second-stage delivery platform that runs arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of every anonymous visitor to an infected site, routes that traffic through the victim’s own domain, and lies dormant for logged-in users. In addition to files following this naming pattern, the plugin also contains files with randomized 8-character long names. We first recovered this malware during two incident response engagements, in January 2026 and September 2026. Those two malware cleanups are the source of this technical analysis. Two malware detection signatures were developed and released after undergoing our QA process on October 16, 2026. All Wordfence Premium , Wordfence Care , and Wordfence Response customers received these signatures immediately. Users of the free version of Wordfence received these signatures on November 15, 2026. As part of our product lineup, we offer security monitoring and malware removal services for our Wordfence Care and Wordfence Response customers. f227832c9e17936d119da406.title_original: How to compare MDR providers when every proposal looks promising
f227832c9e17936d119da406.excerpt: Choosing a managed detection and response (MDR) provider means committing budget, connecting systems, and trusting another team to act when your organization is under pressure. Yet a proposal promising 24x7 coverage, expert analysts, and fast response can leave important questions unanswered. Which systems will actually be monitored? What will analysts investigate before contacting you? What happens when an incident needs more work? Before choosing a provider or renewing your current agreement, ask for evidence of how the service operates. Rapid7’s MDR Evaluation Scorecard gives you 18 checks to structure that conversation and record what still needs proving. Start with one investigation Ask a provider to walk you through a completed investigation, using an anonymized example where necessary. Follow the initial signal through the evidence considered, the analyst’s decision, and any response actions. Suppose suspicious activity involves an account with access to a critical business system. Can the provider show how the account’s permissions, the systems within reach, and known weaknesses influenced its investigation? Can it explain what it ruled out and why it escalated or contained the activity? This exercise helps you assess whether exposure context, intelligence, and customer telemetry work together.
